papers.title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
alternate_titles: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
papers.abstract: Language model (LM) alignment improves model outputs to reflect human preferences while preserving the capabilities of the base model. The most common alignment approaches are (i) reinforcement learning, which maximizes the expected reward under a KL-divergence constraint, and (ii) best-of-NNN alignment, which selects the highest-reward output among NNN independent samples. Despite their widespread use, the fundamental limits of reward improvement under a KL budget remain poorly understood. We characterize the information-theoretic limits of KL-regularized alignment by deriving the maximum…

papers.title: How to grade the accuracy of the BLAS
alternate_titles: How to grade the accuracy of the BLAS
papers.abstract: Motivated by accelerating machine learning (ML), many computer vendors are building accelerators for matrix multiplication, which save time and energy by operating in lower precisions needed for ML. This has in turn motivated many efforts to use these accelerators to provide faster matrix multiplication implementations with the higher precision required by many other linear algebra applications. Motivated by the large design space of algorithms for approximating higher precision, with significant performance/accuracy tradeoffs, we provide a metric to “grade the accuracy” of a matrix multiplication implementation (or the BLAS more generally), ranging from an “A” for attaining the classic floating point error bound, to a “C” for attaining a weaker but still useful bound, that is satisfied by Strassen-like algorithms. We also propose “ungameable” tests that vendors or users can run to verif...

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning to Rank Using Coarse-grained Rewards
alternate_titles: Reinforcement Learning to Rank Using Coarse-grained Rewards
papers.abstract: Learning to rank (LTR) plays a crucial role in various Information Retrieval (IR) tasks. Although supervised LTR methods based on fine-grained relevance labels (e.g., document-level annotations) have achieved significant success, their reliance on costly and potentially biased annotations limits scalability and alignment with realistic goals. In contrast, coarse-grained feedback signals, such as duration time and session-level engagement, are more accessible and affordable. Reinforcement Learning (RL) offers a promising framework to directly optimize these objectives using reward signals, but most existing Reinforcement Learning to Rank (RLTR) approaches suffer from high variance and low sample efficiency. papers.title: Where the World went Missing: Geographic Inequality in Wikipedia and AI
alternate_titles: Where the World went Missing: Geographic Inequality in Wikipedia and AI
papers.abstract: Abstract Wikipedia is among the world’s most important public knowledge datasets and a foundational source for search engines, maps, knowledge graphs, and AI systems, including LLMs. Geographic gaps in coverage may therefore influence what downstream systems can retrieve, infer, and represent. We analyzed 21,270,978 geotagged records across 355 Wikipedia language editions by combining coordinates extracted from article wikitext and Wikidata. We release the dataset and interactive visualization as open resources for research on geographic representation and knowledge inequality. The Global North contained 275.6 records per 1,000 km², compared with 79.0 in the Global South, a density ratio of 3.49. Although this ratio declined from 5.60 in 2010 to 3.49 in 2026, it remained substantial and relatively stable over the past decade. To examine whether this was reflected in AI performance, we as...

papers.title: When Scammers Talk Back: Understanding Potentially Unwanted Calls via LLM-Based Interaction
alternate_titles: When Scammers Talk Back: Understanding Potentially Unwanted Calls via LLM-Based Interaction
papers.abstract: Despite stricter regulations being gradually enforced in telecommunications, potentially unwanted calls (PUCs), including telemarketing and vishing, remain a persistent and evolving threat. However, understanding how PUCs operate in practice has been limited by the lack of real-world datasets with rich conversational content, hindering the development of effective defenses. To fill this gap, we developed an LLM-based phone call honeypot for collecting real-world PUCs, to our knowledge among the first systems to collect such data in the wild. Based on the development, we conducted thematic analysis on 115 hours of conversations collected over 20 months, where we understand how PUCs operate in practice by studying the conversational structure, content, and campaign operations. papers.title: LightShift: Infinite Relighting via Real-time Diffusion Renderer
alternate_titles: LightShift: Infinite Relighting via Real-time Diffusion Renderer
papers.abstract: We present LightShift, a text-driven diffusion framework for real-time streaming video relighting. Unlike reconstruction-based pipelines and methods that require per-video optimization or explicit lighting parameters, LightShift directly maps natural-language descriptions to spatially coherent illumination changes while preserving scene content. We first train a bidirectional relighting model on a large-scale corpus of paired source and synthetically relit videos. We then convert it into an efficient streaming generator through causal-attention adaptation, two-step consistency distillation, and distribution matching distillation with self-rollout. A bounded rolling attention window maintains long-range lighting context with constant per-frame computation, enabling continuous processing independent of video length. On a single NVIDIA RTX 4090, LightShift processes 576×1024 videos at over...

papers.title: From World Foundation Models to Real-world applications: An Introduction
alternate_titles: From World Foundation Models to Real-world applications: An Introduction
papers.abstract: This course introduces the emerging paradigm of world foundation models (WFMs) and their role in enabling real-world physical AI systems. Those WFMs learn structured, multimodal representations of physical environments, supporting perception, prediction, and decision-making from a shared representation that spans vision, language, and action. The course connects foundation model concepts to dynamic visual environments, simulation, synthetic data generation, robotics, and sim-to-real deployment.

papers.abstract: Abstract Static Application Security Testing tools trace untrusted data flows using curated lists of Security-Relevant Methods (SRMs), namely sources, sinks and sanitizers. Machine learning approaches for SRM detection (ML4SRM) report strong cross-validation results yet perform far worse on unseen code, and prior work has not asked why. To assess this disparity we develop WEAVE, a tool combining automated model selection, repeated cross-validation and explainable Artificial intelligence (XAI) using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for WEKA/MEKA pipelines. Using WEAVE and SRM-Dataset, our consolidated collection of 10{,}180 Java SRMs, we conduct an explanation study of three ML4SRM approaches, namely, Dev-Assist, SSCM, and SWAN. alternate_titles: Turning Multi-Agent Communication into Token-Level Credit with On Policy Self Distillation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning improves problem solving in large language model multi-agent systems. Existing approaches overlook communication knowledge or compress it into scalar rewards, leaving coarse credit with little guidance on which decisions each agent should reinforce or revise. OPSD4MAS converts future communication into fine-grained token-level credit through On Policy Self Distillation (OPSD). alternate_titles: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
papers.abstract: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. alternate_titles: Split-and-scale Latent 3D Representations
papers.abstract: Latent 3D representations have significantly expanded the capabilities of modern shape modeling, enabling compact encoding of 3D scenes and supporting powerful 3D generative models. Despite this progress, current representations struggle to capture the fine details of complex objects, fundamentally limited by the capacity of their latents. However, scaling latent capacity at training time is computationally expensive and often infeasible under memory limits, and naively increasing the number of latents at inference fails to make effective use of the added capacity. alternate_titles: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories is a standard paradigm for training LLM agents. However, it suffers from a well-known training-inference distribution mismatch, calling for target-aware data synthesis strategies that ground the training data in the target model's native state distribution. To bridge this gap, emerging approaches incorporate the expert either to guide mixed rollouts alongside the target model, or to provide dense step-wise supervision. Nonetheless, existing methods apply expert assistance blind to the target model's inherent behavior: they either disrupt the rollout using sub-optimal random intervention heuristics, or they enforce indiscriminate uniform supervision that unnecessarily overwrites the model's already-correct actions. alternate_titles: TerraLingua: Open-ended Emergence of Societies in an LLM Ecology
papers.abstract: Abstract Artifacts that persist across generations---such as monuments, technologies, and texts---catalyze major developments in human societies. Can artifacts have a similar impact in AI-based societies? This paper introduces (1) TerraLingua, a many-agent world where agents have limited lifespans and resources, but can build artifacts that outlive their creators; and (2) an AI Anthropologist that characterizes the rich societal dynamics that emerge. With these tools, it is possible to answer a well-known conjecture in open-ended AI: artifacts are critical to sustained complex development. Blocking artifacts produces shallow cultural lineages and more frequent aggression, whereas instructions to maximize artifacts may lead to population collapse. alternate_titles: Composing Lightweight Methods on Deep Neural Network: A Survey
papers.abstract: Abstract Deep learning has achieved remarkable progress across many domains, largely powered by large-scale neural networks. Their substantial computational demands, however, hinder deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this, lightweight techniques, such as efficient architecture design, pruning, quantization, decomposition, and knowledge distillation, have been explored to reduce the required resources while preserving accuracy. While prior surveys typically investigate these methods one by one, limited attention has been given to how their composition, ordering, and optimization dependencies affect efficiency and accuracy in real-world settings. Exploiting this performance advantage while preserving the numerical accuracy required in quantum chemistry remains a significant challenge. papers.title: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Systems
alternate_titles: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Systems
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of Large Language Model (LLM) inference systems has led to significant improvements in serving efficiency. papers.abstract: Reproducible evaluation, verifiable inference and on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) need an LLM engine to give a request the same output bits whichever requests share its batch. Batch-invariant kernels exist, but engines still select each kernel and its parameters from the batch. Two kernels that compute the same sum can round it differently. papers.title: BAmbiDrop: Array-Agnostic Speech Enhancement with Zero-Shot binaural Reproduction using Multi-center Ambisonics Encoding
alternate_titles: BAmbiDrop: Array-Agnostic Speech Enhancement with Zero-Shot binaural Reproduction using Multi-center Ambisonics Encoding
papers.abstract: Array-agnostic enhancement networks generalize across microphone geometries but produce a single channel, while binaural enhancement methods preserve interaural cues only for one fixed device geometry. We propose BAmbiDrop, a framework that extends array-agnostic enhancement to binaural reproduction without retraining. Exploiting the fact that the Ambisonics origin is an arbitrary point in space, a frozen single-channel AmbiDrop network estimates a complex mask at multiple centers across the array; these masks are fused by a complex mean into a single shared mask, applied to the microphone signals and rendered by fixed BSM filters. Across 21 free-field and rigid-sphere arrays, the fused mask improves enhancement and interaural cue reproduction simultaneously, whereas masking each microphone independently degrades the latter without a consistent gain in the former.

papers.abstract: Human cognition is fundamentally driven by a bilateral synergy loop, where multimodal understanding (MMU) and generation interleave and reinforce each other. This observation motivates Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) to foster bilateral synergy across multiple dimensions, such as data and architecture. However, existing methods typically explore these dimensions in isolation and remain confined to limited training stages, leaving the hierarchical role of interleaving in advancing holistic bilateral synergy largely underexplored. To this end, we propose SAIL-Unify, a new UMM that systematically explores the synergistic gains of hierarchical interleaving across data, architectural design, learning strategies, and shared policy optimization throughout the full lifecycle of pre-training and post-training. Specifically, we first unify data formats and establish dual-track pipelines for rigor...

papers.title: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers
alternate_titles: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers
papers.abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) extends RL with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks by scoring each response against query-specific rubrics. Under group-relative optimization, however, a rubric that every sampled response fails (unreachable) or passes (saturated) gives all responses the same outcome and no learning signal; in Qwen3-4B medical training, 60.88% of query-rubric observations are inactive. We find that the two states lack different supervision: stating an unreachable rubric in the prompt raises its satisfaction from 1.13% to 91.25%, whereas responses that all pass a saturated rubric still differ in quality. We therefore propose RuACT (Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers), which assigns each inactive rubric the role that supplies what it lacks. papers.title: Rethinking Low-Frequency Bias in Transformers for Crowd Localization
alternate_titles: Rethinking Low-Frequency Bias in Transformers for Crowd Localization
papers.abstract: Vision Transformers exhibit strong global modeling capabilities in crowd localization, yet their efficiency-oriented self-attention designs introduce a low-frequency bias. This suppresses high-frequency details, leading to over-smoothed responses and degraded instance separability. To address this issue, a Frequency-aware Attention Network (FANet) is proposed to jointly model global low-frequency semantics and local high-frequency structures. At its core, a frequency-aware dual-branch transformer module is designed, which is composed of three key components. First, a local-enhanced attention branch is designed alongside the global branch to recover fine-grained high-frequency details at the original resolution. Furthermore, to enable effective integration of complementary frequency components, an adaptive frequency gating mechanism is developed to perform spatially selective and adaptive...

papers.title: Rethinking Latent Reasoning for Generative Recommendation: Beyond Teacher-Generated CoT and Recurrent Hidden-State Feedback
alternate_titles: Rethinking Latent Reasoning for Generative Recommendation: Beyond Teacher-Generated CoT and Recurrent Hidden-State Feedback
papers.abstract: Latent reasoning in generative recommendation faces two practical barriers: constructing teacher-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision is costly, and recurrent hidden-state feedback requires a specialized execution loop. We revisit both the supervision source and the computation interface. A step-level diagnosis measures how recommendation CoT supports next-item prediction and trace coherence. In the analyzed traces, history analysis is the only step with positive mean contributions on both dimensions, while later preference and intent steps have negative mean answer contributions. Guided by this finding, we propose PHiT (Prefilled, History-Informed Thought Tokens), which learns intermediate states from semantic targets extracted directly from observed item histories. PHiT aggregates cached sparse item encodings to construct these targets and supervises the contextual states of di...

papers.title: Rectifying and Consolidating Latent Diffusion for Remote Sensing Object Detection
alternate_titles: Rectifying and Consolidating Latent Diffusion for Remote Sensing Object Detection
papers.abstract: Remote sensing object detection is fundamentally challenged by scale variations and background clutter. Existing discriminative methods often lack the generative comprehension needed to interpret ambiguous objects from incomplete visual cues. While adapting text-to-image diffusion models offers rich semantic priors to bridge this gap, their application is limited by a dual dissonance: semantic manifold misalignment and generative temporal trajectory underutilization. In this paper, we propose rectified consolidated latent diffusion (RCLD), a novel generative-perception framework. Firstly, we present a semantic manifold rectification to purify the semantic space. It uses a learnable latent probe to dynamically filter out irrelevant text embeddings, thereby restricting multi-modal interactions to the valid scene subspace. Then we propose a temporal trajectory consolidation to integrate the...

papers.title: Real-Time Co-Speech Gesture Video Generation
alternate_titles: Real-Time Co-Speech Gesture Video Generation
papers.abstract: Co-speech gesture video generation aims to create realistic videos of speakers where facial expressions and body movements are naturally synchronized with the speech audio. An effective system must reconcile two often-conflicting objectives: a) real-time performance, which is crucial for interactive applications, and b) high-fidelity synthesis, ensuring photorealism and natural motion. While impressive progress has been made, most methods excel at one at the expense of the other. To bridge this gap, we present a two-stage framework that achieves zero-shot high-fidelity synthesis while operating in real-time. Our approach strategically employs lightweight 2D upper-body keypoints as an efficient intermediate representation, decoupling the task into two stages. First, a motion generation module predicts precise 2D keypoints from the audio input, explicitly capturing its rhythm and semantic...

papers.title: RadAR: Accelerating Autoregressive Visual Generation with Radial Decoding
alternate_titles: RadAR: Accelerating Autoregressive Visual Generation with Radial Decoding
papers.abstract: Inspired by the remarkable success of autoregressive models in language modeling, this paradigm has been widely adopted in visual generation. However, the sequential token-by-token decoding mechanism inherent in traditional autoregressive models leads to low inference efficiency. In this paper, we propose RadAR, an efficient and parallelizable framework designed to accelerate autoregressive visual generation while preserving its representational capacity. Our approach is motivated by the observation that visual tokens exhibit strong local dependencies and spatial correlations with their neighbors—a property not fully exploited in standard raster-scan decoding orders. papers.title: Query-Guided RoPE Modulation for Lost-in-the-Middle Mitigation in Long-Context LLMs
alternate_titles: Query-Guided RoPE Modulation for Lost-in-the-Middle Mitigation in Long-Context LLMs
papers.abstract: Long-context language models often neglect information in the middle of the input, a phenomenon known as "lost-in-the-middle". Part of this gap may stem from the long-range decay of rotary position embedding (RoPE), which weakens the positional signal between distant tokens. Existing input compression deletes low-importance tokens, and attention reweighting acts only after RoPE has weakened this signal. RoPE-level methods modify positions directly but apply the same remapping to every query. To address these limitations, we propose QGPM (Query-Guided Positional Modulation), a training-free method that reshapes RoPE positions using query relevance from the model's own attention heads. QGPM builds a broad relevance map for lower layers and a sharp one for upper layers. alternate_titles: Probing Human-Centric Rule-based Reasoning Abilities of Video Generation Models for Vision Foundation Intelligence
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have enabled the synthesis of videos with strong temporal consistency and impressive visual quality. As these perceptual capabilities continue to improve, the next critical challenge toward vision foundation models is to equip models with more robust reasoning abilities for generating coherent and logically consistent video dynamics. Recently, several benchmarks have been proposed to assess the reasoning abilities of video generation models, most of which primarily focus on visual transformations and physics-aware reasoning (e.g., gravity, fluid dynamics), while largely lacking a human-centric perspective in their evaluations. To address this gap, we introduce RULER-Bench, a benchmark grounded in a cognitive rule-based formulation. papers.title: PersonaRL: Unleashing and Benchmarking Personalized Understanding via Unified Reinforcement Learning and Dataset
alternate_titles: PersonaRL: Unleashing and Benchmarking Personalized Understanding via Unified Reinforcement Learning and Dataset
papers.abstract: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated exceptional general reasoning, they often fail in personalized scenarios due to three fundamental challenges: (i) data noise and heterogeneity in raw user traces, (ii) the entanglement of soft aesthetic preferences with hard objective constraints, and (iii) the inherent difficulty of high-dimensional subjective alignment. To address these issues, we propose PersonaRL, a unified reinforcement learning framework for subjective multimodal personalization. We first design a Multi-Agent Data Process Pipeline that employs specialized agents for preference analysis and query rewriting, systematically transforming scattered user inputs into standardized training signals. papers.title: Peak-End-Net: A Peak-End Rule Inspired Framework for Generalizable Video Aesthetic Assessment
alternate_titles: Peak-End-Net: A Peak-End Rule Inspired Framework for Generalizable Video Aesthetic Assessment
papers.abstract: Video aesthetic assessment (VAA) aims to predict how aesthetically pleasing a video is, yet remains far less explored than other visual assessment tasks. Its progress is hindered not only by the scarcity of large-scale benchmarks, but also by the intrinsic subjectivity of aesthetic judgment, which is shaped by human perception. In this paper, we revisit VAA from a psychological perspective and propose Peak-End-Net, a lightweight and interpretable framework inspired by the peak-end rule, which suggests that people tend to judge a temporal experience mainly according to its salient moments and the ending. Building on this intuition, we first transfer knowledge from image aesthetic assessment (IAA) to VAA by introducing a pretrained IAA head to produce frame-wise aesthetic priors, which serve as surrogate signals for identifying aesthetically salient moments and guiding peak-end rule-based...

papers.title: PBU-ReCab: Partial Backbone Unfreezing and Retrospective Calibration for Domain-Incremental Object Detection
alternate_titles: PBU-ReCab: Partial Backbone Unfreezing and Retrospective Calibration for Domain-Incremental Object Detection
papers.abstract: Domain-Incremental Object Detection (DIOD) requires a detector to continuously adapt to new visual domains while retaining performance on all previously encountered domains. To resolve the stability--plasticity trade-off, existing approaches usually assign and train a new set of parameters for each new domain while freezing the backbone and the parameters for earlier domains. Although freezing the backbone eliminates disturbance to learned domains, it severely restricts the model's ability to learn from new ones. Conversely, allowing the backbone to be freely updated enables it to capture new information but often degrades the representations needed for old domains. To tackle this dilemma, we propose a Partial Backbone Unfreezing-Retro-Calibration framework (PBU-ReCab) for DIOD. papers.title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
alternate_titles: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
papers.abstract: 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns a shared latent space that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs, allowing data-rich geometric and visual priors to support data-scarce part learning. Given a single input image, the base model generates geometry, deformation, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset without a separate segmentation stage. papers.title: NexusQA: Spatio-Temporal Interlacement Grounded VideoQA
alternate_titles: NexusQA: Spatio-Temporal Interlacement Grounded VideoQA
papers.abstract: Video question answering (VideoQA) requires sophisticated interpretation of spatio-temporal dynamics. While grounded VideoQA has emerged to provide verifiable evidence, existing benchmarks are predominantly confined to Coarse-grained Spatio-Temporal (CST) evidence, such as event or object-level localization. Consequently, they fail to scrutinize the Fine-grained Spatio-Temporal (FST) evidence essential for clarifying subtle semantic states, allowing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to exploit language priors instead of performing genuine visual grounding. To address this, we introduce NexusBench, a novel benchmark requiring joint reasoning across Multi-grained Spatio-Temporal evidence. Built upon a Hierarchical Video Scene Graph (HVSG), it explicitly models FST interactions to build logic-intensive queries. alternate_titles: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
papers.abstract: LLM agents benefit from using memory systems to improve performance on long-horizon, multi-session tasks. However, memory introduces a critical attack surface. Malicious instructions encountered in one session may be stored and propagated through memory before being retrieved and acted upon in later sessions. Because memory systems differ in how they process and retrieve information, the downstream effects of poisoning can vary significantly across systems. To quantify the effects of poisoning across different memory architectures, we introduce MemoryDojo, a benchmark for tracing the lifecycle of poisoned information through agent memory and measuring its influence on subsequent agent behavior. papers.abstract: Multi-vector retrieval represents each query and document as a set of embeddings and scores relevance via fine-grained set-to-set interactions such as MaxSim (Chamfer similarity). This expressiveness improves retrieval quality over single-vector representations, but makes search substantially more expensive. Existing systems address this challenge primarily through proxy representations or filter-and-rerank pipelines that reduce candidate generation to single-vector search. alternate_titles: MESS: Deep Reasoning and Multimodal Agentic Framework for Evolutionary Survey Synthesis
papers.abstract: Crafting high-quality scientific surveys demands not only profound literature insights but also intuitive, professional diagrams to facilitate comprehension. However, existing automated survey generation systems predominantly rely on shallow retrieval and mere information stacking across massive literature, failing to uncover the intrinsic logic of technological evolution. Furthermore, these systems are incapable of producing expert-level academic diagrams, resulting in significant limitations in both content depth and visual representation within the generated surveys. To address these critical gaps, we propose the Deep Reasoning and Multimodal Agentic Framework for Evolutionary Survey Synthesis (MESS). papers.title: MARS: Training Multilingual Search Agents for Retriever-Free Evidence Acquisition
alternate_titles: MARS: Training Multilingual Search Agents for Retriever-Free Evidence Acquisition

In this paper, we explore retriever-free multilingual search, where the model directly interacts with raw corpora through executable shell commands. This paradigm shifts the bottleneck to multilingual search action generation, where exact search is sensitive to entity surface forms and outcome-only supervision provides limited guidance for multi-turn search. To address these challenges, we propose MARS, a multilingual search agent in direct corpus interaction (DCI) with reinforcement learning (RL). We combine these three outputs through one fitted conditional average treatment effect (CATE) model. Stable Causal Rule Learning (SCRL) produces concise subgroup descriptions using empirical treatment–control support checks and a bootstrap‐based score. Constrained feature‐space recourse searches for higher predicted CATE under permitted coordinate changes. papers.title: GSynPEF: A Privacy Evaluation Framework for Synthetic Graphs
alternate_titles: GSynPEF: A Privacy Evaluation Framework for Synthetic Graphs
papers.abstract: It is often desirable to generate and release synthetic graphs, which resemble real-world data, in a privacy-preserving way. While substantial progress has been made in designing private graph synthesizers (PGS), opportunities remain for more explicit connections between synthesizer models and privacy evaluation, and better accounting for output variation. This paper proposes GSynPEF, a practical framework for empirical evaluation of privacy and utility in settings for which a real-world graph is given as input and output synthetic graph(s) are observed. Our framework links a broad class of graph synthesizers (both statistical and deep-learning based) with privacy metrics, expanding evaluation dimensions to practical utility and risk, through empirical analysis of multiple actual outputs. papers.title: From Structure to Details: Asynchronous Diffusion Refinement for Multispectral and Panchromatic Image Fusion

papers.abstract: Diffusion model based fusion of low-resolution multispectral (LRMS) and panchromatic (PAN) images has attracted increasing attention in recent years. However, most existing methods jointly treat PAN and multispectral images as conditions to the denoising network without explicitly distinguishing their distinct roles in the fusion process. As a result, the model is unable to impose differentiated constraints and guidance, leading to unsatisfactory spectral information preservation and spatial detail enhancement. Recent advancements have demonstrated that diffusion models tend to generate overall structures in the initial denoising stages and then progressively recover fine details in latter stages. papers.title: From Discord to Accord: A Consensus-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Multi-Modal Question Answering
alternate_titles: From Discord to Accord: A Consensus-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Multi-Modal Question Answering
papers.abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) integrate heterogeneous inputs to solve tasks that require joint reasoning across modalities, such as multi-modal question answering (MQA). Existing multi-agent methods are largely inspired by individual-level cognitive mechanisms (e.g., fast-slow thinking and metacognition), but often under-exploit social cognitive factors that govern how groups reconcile disagreements. The time-series foundation model TimesFM maintained comparatively stable probabilistic forecast performance at longer horizons, while most other models showed declining performance. papers.title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models?

papers.abstract: Benchmark gains from reasoning-enhanced large language models encourage the assumption that these models should broadly perform better on complex generative tasks, but this remains underexplored in open-ended, creative domains shaped by nuances of reader experience. papers.title: Disentangling Instruction Influence in Diffusion Transformers for Parallel Multi-Instruction-Guided Image Editing
alternate_titles: Disentangling Instruction Influence in Diffusion Transformers for Parallel Multi-Instruction-Guided Image Editing
papers.abstract: Instruction-guided image editing allows users to specify modifications in natural language. Recent advances show that Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) surpass U-Net-based diffusion models in both scalability and performance. However, real-world scenarios often involve applying multiple instructions simultaneously. Step-by-step editing accumulates errors and degrades image quality, while putting all instructions into a single prompt typically leads to incomplete edits. To address these challenges, we introduce Instruction Influence Disentanglement (IID), a training-free framework that enables simultaneous handling of multiple instructions within a single denoising process for DiT-based models. papers.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI

papers.abstract: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. alternate_titles: Continuous Masked Diffusion for Autonomous Driving

papers.abstract: We present a unified potential method for contextual search and bilateral trade with one-bit feedback and obtain order-tight algorithms for both problems. Our framework starts from a Bayesian perspective in which the unknown target (for contextual search) and the unknown pair of valuations (for bilateral trade) are sampled from a known prior distribution. In that model, the decision maker bases its prediction on the posterior distribution, obtained by conditioning on feedback received in previous rounds. For Bayesian contextual search, we present an algorithm with a total loss bounded by $O(\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt Σ)$, where $Σ$ is the covariance matrix of the target's prior; and for contextual bilateral trade, our algorithm's regret is bounded by $O(\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt{Σ_S}+\mathrm{Tr} \sqrt{Σ_B})$, where $Σ_S$ and $Σ_B$ are the covariance matrices of the seller's and buyer's valuations. alternate_titles: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
papers.abstract: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. alternate_titles: BayesCrop: Real-Time Probabilistic Multi-Crop Video Reframing
papers.abstract: Automatic video reframing is increasingly important for adapting landscape content to heterogeneous display formats. Existing methods typically predict a single deterministic crop, despite the subjective nature of reframing and the presence of multiple plausible regions of interest. We present \textbf{BayesCrop}, a real-time probabilistic framework for multi-crop video reframing. BayesCrop represents crop preferences using a two-component spatially isotropic Gaussian mixture over crop position and scale. Each component defines a representative reframing mode together with its local uncertainty, enabling both dual-view prediction and sampling of additional plausible crop candidates. alternate_titles: BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization
papers.abstract: Automated harness optimization improves agents by learning from trajectories and task feedback. Existing offline methods use reference answers to optimize harnesses for reuse on held-out tasks. However, many real-world tasks are open-ended, while long runs expose new difficulties that offline-optimized harnesses may not address. To study harness optimization in these settings, we introduce PerfRace, a benchmark for long-running performance optimization of software projects, and investigate whether agents can use task-specific experience to recursively improve their harnesses during an ongoing task. To this end, we introduce BOXBOX, which enables agent-triggered harness revision and kernel-managed hot reloading while preserving execution context. papers.abstract: We present the Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline (ASP), an offline rollout scheduler for multi-instance asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) of large language models (LLMs). This enables efficient multi-instance rollout that overcomes the early scaling plateau of single-instance inference while reducing fluctuations in the supply of generated samples to the trainer. papers.abstract: High-performance image-text retrieval (ITR) relies on large-scale multimodal data with fine-grained semantic alignment, yet real-world data exhibits pronounced cross-modal information asymmetry: images are often rich while texts are sparse or ambiguous, leading to biased representations and unstable retrieval. To address this, we propose AIM (Asymmetry-aware Information Modeling), an information-theoretic framework that explicitly models and exploits modality asymmetry via a unified information signal. Our metric jointly captures information deficiency (through directional likelihood gaps from InfoNCE) and information ambiguity (via entropy-based uncertainty), yielding a sample-wise estimate of information gain. papers.abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the workplace has raised questions about how employer demand for different work activities is changing. We examine how the prevalence and content of work activities in online job postings change in association with activity-level measures of AI exposure, derived from Copilot and Claude usage. To enable systematic comparisons, we develop a pipeline that extracts the responsibilities from job advertisements and maps them onto O*NET's standardized taxonomy of Intermediate Work Activities (IWAs). We then apply this approach to 50,000 job advertisements from 33 firms between 2023 and 2025. alternate_titles: SIFR: Stable Signed Flow Reinforcement
papers.abstract: Reward-based fine-tuning of flow models requires effectively promoting high-reward and suppressing low-reward samples, while maintaining training stability over many rounds of iterative updates. Iterative reward fine-tuning provides a simple starting point, but the positive reward weights give no explicit unfitting signal, and repeated reweighting concentrates the distribution and causes collapse. We propose Stable Signed Flow Reinforcement (SIFR), which replaces the reward weights by signed advantages to supply the missing unfitting signal, and constrains the velocity drift from a reference model to stabilize the updates, with a Lagrange multiplier that adapts the regularization strength to a prescribed drift budget. papers.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
alternate_titles: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
papers.abstract: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies. papers.title: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
alternate_titles: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
papers.abstract: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. In our experiments, a model fine-tuned only on a "poison" dataset associated with a trait T (such as speaking German or being misaligned) does not learn T. Surprisingly, adding similarly formatted "clean" data not associated with T causes the model to learn T. This effect requires that the poison data have an identifying "trigger" feature that is absent from the clean data. We demonstrate this effect in a variety of settings: subliminal learning of backdoor behaviors, inoculation prompting of reward hacking transcripts, generalization from archaic bird names, and an MNIST classifier with mislabeled data. papers.abstract: Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs) decompose the activations of large language models into human-interpretable features and trace how these features interact across layers to form circuits, making them a key tool for mechanistic interpretability. Beyond the usual trade-off between sparsity and reconstruction quality, a CLT has to model all layers at once, which adds a further challenge. The common JumpReLU recipe controls sparsity only indirectly through a penalty, while the direct extension of TopK selects a fixed number of latents in every layer. alternate_titles: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
papers.abstract: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. Conventional post-training pipelines that apply SFT sequentially before RL are not architected for this regime: their uniform treatment of task distributions suppresses underrepresented capabilities and exacerbates catastrophic forgetting in data-sparse tasks. papers.title: SMP Challenge - Social Media Popularity Prediction for Images and Videos
alternate_titles: SMP Challenge - Social Media Popularity Prediction for Images and Videos
papers.abstract: Social media popularity prediction aims to estimate future user engagement from multimedia content, user information, and temporal context. The Social Media Prediction (SMP) Challenge provides benchmark datasets and evaluation protocols for this task. This year, we organize two tracks: SMP-Image for image posts and SMP-Video for short-form videos. The new Video Track responds to the growing prevalence of short-form video and to recent advances in vision-language models that extract semantic and temporal cues from dynamic content. We release the Social Media Prediction Dataset (SMPD), providing image and video benchmarks with online leaderboards for both tracks. This paper also summarizes the principal technical trends according to the challenge solutions.

papers.abstract: Language agents increasingly use persistent memory to record user preferences and procedures across sessions. We show that memory from benign interactions can cause unsafe or unreliable behavior on later tasks. We call this failure the memory trap. papers.abstract: Camera-controllable video generation aims to synthesize videos with flexible and physically plausible camera movements. To address these issues, we propose a novel Vision-Language-Camera model, termed CT-1 (Camera Transformer 1), a specialized model designed to transfer spatial reasoning knowledge to video generation by accurately estimating camera trajectories. Built upon vision-language modules and a Diffusion Transformer model, CT-1 employs a Wavelet-based Regularization Loss in the frequency domain to effectively learn complex camera trajectory distributions. These trajectories are integrated into a video diffusion model to enable spatially aware camera control that aligns with user intentions. T...

papers.title: zkARc: Succinctly Verifiable Proofs for Neurosymbolic Natural Language Formalization and Verification
alternate_titles: zkARc: Succinctly Verifiable Proofs for Neurosymbolic Natural Language Formalization and Verification
papers.abstract: Autonomous agents increasingly execute consequential actions on behalf of users, but ordinary middleware guardrails do not provide cryptographic proof that a policy was actually enforced. Their verdicts leave counterparties dependent on the operator unless they repeat the checks themselves, potentially exposing sensitive policies and inputs. We present zkARc, a modular proof-carrying framework that wraps each stage of Automated Reasoning checks (ARc) in an independent, succinctly verifiable zero-knowledge proof. ARc is a neurosymbolic system that translates natural language policies into formal logic and verifies AI-generated content against them using SMT solvers. zkARc certifies the planner's output, the policy's formalization, the action's formalization and both solver queries. The receipt binds these computations to the exact action received and, under the stated assumptions, reveals...

papers.title: When Bigger Becomes Brittle: Why Compression Hurts More as Language Models Scale
alternate_titles: When Bigger Becomes Brittle: Why Compression Hurts More as Language Models Scale
papers.abstract: Quantization and pruning reduce the cost of deploying language models, but their effects are usually reported as benchmark scores. Such scores record only the loss that remains at the output. Inside the model, compression damages some components more than others, and the rest of the network can partly compensate. The observed loss therefore reflects both the damage and this compensation, which benchmark scores cannot separate. How the two combine, and whether their balance changes with model size, remains unclear. We study this compensation for in-context retrieval, a capability carried by a small, identifiable set of attention heads. To separate the two, the expected loss from ablating these heads is decomposed exactly into the part restored by the rest of the network, attributed to the components responsible, and the part that reaches the output. papers.title: What Gets Hacked in a Collaborative Reward for LLM Recommenders: The Part That Does Not Depend on the User
alternate_titles: What Gets Hacked in a Collaborative Reward for LLM Recommenders: The Part That Does Not Depend on the User
papers.abstract: Collaborative-filtering (CF) scores provide graded, personalized rewards for training large language model (LLM) recommenders through reinforcement learning. However, these rewards can cause exposure collapse: even though the CF model itself produces diverse top recommendations across users, an LLM optimized with its rewards concentrates on fewer items. We decompose each score into an item-mean component, the item's average CF score across user histories, and a residual component, the current user's score deviation from the average. Through controlled interventions, we identify the item-mean component as a contributor to exposure collapse. Accordingly, we propose two reward corrections: per-item centering removes each item's estimated mean score, while per-item standardization further rescales the residual using its estimated standard deviation. Experiments on two datasets with two ident...

papers.title: WARP: Workload-Aware Residual Profiling for Graph-Equivalent Recommender Inference
alternate_titles: WARP: Workload-Aware Residual Profiling for Graph-Equivalent Recommender Inference
papers.abstract: Hardware-aware graph optimization can accelerate recommender inference, but choosing among equivalent execution plans is vulnerable to inaccurate cost estimates and noisy microbenchmarks. We instantiate the bandwidth-ratio, roofline-plus-dispatch plan-ranking mechanism of the CAGR framework as the analytical prior of an executable selector and extend it with two-parameter residual calibration by batch size and categorical access context. Six equivalent embedding/interactions plans are validated numerically and evaluated using frozen parameters on synthetic CPU request streams. In an initial 16-context study, the calibrated selector reaches 2.55× geometric-mean speedup against an unfused eager reference and reduces the held-out latency-prediction error of the CAGR-style prior from 57.2% to 12.6%. A stronger fixed TorchScript baseline, however, achieves 2.60× in those same observations. We...

papers.title: Video * Bench: Benchmarking Fine-grained Video Perception with "Think with Videos"
alternate_titles: Video * Bench: Benchmarking Fine-grained Video Perception with "Think with Videos"
papers.abstract: Interactive agents need fine-grained long-video understanding. Current Video-LLMs remain brittle when relevant evidence is subtle or sparse. Fixed frame budgets force rich streams into a few sampled frames and often discard decisive cues. We introduce Video* Bench, a benchmark with 2,212 real-world videos and ten tasks spanning content, semantic, and spatio-temporal perception. Its low Detail Index emphasizes sparse, localized evidence. We evaluate 33 systems under multiple-choice and open-ended settings. Models recognize appearance and text better but remain weak at temporal localization, duration, and counting; performance also falls as the required detail becomes finer. We further evaluate ''Think-with-Videos'' (TwV) agents that resample frames and perform multi-turn reasoning at fixed budgets. They improve fine-grained and temporal perception without more visual tokens and remain rob...

papers.title: UpCLIP: Upcycling CLIP with Shared and Fine-grained Experts
alternate_titles: UpCLIP: Upcycling CLIP with Shared and Fine-grained Experts
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures provide an effective way to scale model capacity while keeping inference costs manageable. However, training MoE models from scratch typically requires substantial computational resources and often leads to unstable training dynamics. In this work, we present Upcycling CLIP with Shared and Fine-grained Experts, a lightweight framework that upgrades a pretrained CLIP model into a MoE architecture with only a small amount of additional training. Specifically, we introduce a Shared Expert to retain the global representation ability of the original CLIP encoder, while a set of Fine-grained Experts are learned to model diverse visual–textual patterns. We also propose a group-wise expert formulation that ensures structured and balanced activation of fine-grained experts. papers.title: Uncovering Systematic Blind Spots in Graph Database Testing through Integration and Process-Level Analysis
alternate_titles: Uncovering Systematic Blind Spots in Graph Database Testing through Integration and Process-Level Analysis
papers.abstract: Graph databases are becoming foundational infrastructure for connected data, and a growing body of automated testing techniques has uncovered many bugs across mature graph database systems. Each technique checks a different aspect of correctness and exposes a different class of defect. Combining them is the natural next step, but each technique is judged by the real bugs it finds, not by useless reports or tests that can never fail, and that is what decides whether a developer can afford to fix the problems. To identify the remaining gaps, we integrated test capabilities from 8 testing methods and conducted an empirical study of their behavior, during which we found two blind spots. First, 12 hours of testing produce thousands of bug reports, far more than the number of genuine defects a mature database is likely to contain. papers.title: Training-Free Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion
alternate_titles: Training-Free Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk and have made efficient video generation practical. However, further accelerating these models toward real-time generation remains challenging, as few-step distillation leaves little cross-step redundancy for existing training-free caching methods to exploit. We revisit this regime and identify two token-level redundancy patterns: cross-frame redundancy from static content shared across adjacent frames, and cross-step redundancy from tokens that converge early during denoising. Crucially, we find that early clean estimates along the model's own denoising trajectory provide an effective online signal for locating both patterns, requiring no retraining, auxiliary predictor, or reference video. papers.title: Training-Free Image Editing with Visual Context Integration and Concept Alignment
alternate_titles: Training-Free Image Editing with Visual Context Integration and Concept Alignment
papers.abstract: In image editing, it is essential to incorporate a context image to convey the user's precise requirements, such as subject appearance or image style. Existing training-based visual context-aware editing methods incur data collection effort and training cost. On the other hand, the training-free alternatives are typically established on diffusion inversion, which struggles with consistency and flexibility. In this work, we propose VicoEdit, a training-free and inversion-free method to inject the visual context into the pretrained text-prompted editing model. More specifically, VicoEdit directly transforms the source image into the target one based on the visual context, thereby eliminating the need for inversion that can lead to deviated trajectories. papers.title: Training Stability under Adaptive Curricula
alternate_titles: Training Stability under Adaptive Curricula
papers.abstract: Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approaches train reinforcement learning (RL) agents on diverse curricula that may evolve with their capabilities. While prior work has largely focused on how these curricula are constructed, we study whether their students remain trainable under the resulting distributions. Across multiple UED mechanisms, environment complexities, and extended training horizons, we identify recurring learner-side pathologies, including parameter growth, degraded value--outcome ordering, and loss of representational diversity, that accompany stagnation and performance degradation. These findings connect limitations in UED to optimization failures previously identified in conventional deep RL, while showing how adaptive curricula couple the learner's optimization state to its future training distribution. papers.title: The Intrusion Pathway: How Non-Evidential Context Degrades Language Model Performance
alternate_titles: The Intrusion Pathway: How Non-Evidential Context Degrades Language Model Performance
papers.abstract: Language models lose accuracy when a prompt contains non-evidential context: irrelevant statements from unrelated domains, or random off-distribution tokens, with no competing answer and no semantic overlap with the query. Such noise pervades retrieval-augmented, tool-using, and long-context deployments, yet the failure has lacked a mechanistic account. We trace the corruption to the Intrusion Pathway, which starts with MLPs enriching both query-subject and irrelevant-token representations, parroting heads carry prefix-token content to the prediction position, and relational readers largely avoid unrelated sources. Nevertheless, preserved subject enrichment and selective reading do not prevent intrusion in the broader computation. papers.title: The Gating Mechanism of KV Cache Eviction
alternate_titles: The Gating Mechanism of KV Cache Eviction
papers.abstract: KV cache eviction must decide which entries carry information that the rest of the cache can no longer supply. A natural way to estimate this is a learnable gate: give each cached entry a gate on its attention weight and train the gate on the model's own objective. The gate belongs inside the normalizing softmax, where suppressing one entry hands its mass to the others rather than discarding it. That same normalizer absorbs any per-query constant, so a constant gate cancels and reproduces the frozen model exactly. Trained on the language-modeling loss the gate stays near a constant score while its loss falls throughout: optimization succeeds, but a frozen backbone was fit for dense attention, so its loss prefers the no-op, and a near-constant score ranks nothing. papers.title: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs
alternate_titles: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) applied to 3D medical scans face a structural memory wall. A single CT or MRI volume produces tens of thousands of vision tokens, and the resulting key-value (KV) cache scales linearly with both batch and context. Existing KV compression methods operate on the cache's feature or token statistics, or apply 1D and 2D transforms, leaving the three-axis spatial structure in the cache unexploited. We propose TACT-KV (Tri-Axis Cosine Transform), a calibration-free KV compression method that exploits strong spatial correlations in visual KV states along all three anatomical axes of 3D scans. This correlation concentrates the KV cache energy under a frequency-domain transform. papers.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
alternate_titles: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
papers.abstract: We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scales and camera configurations. This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale targets, leading to ambiguous supervision. To address this, we propose SplatAnything with Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. To rigorously assess our method, we further establish a systematic benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and challenging extrapolated viewpoints. papers.title: SpeedyGS: Content-Aware 3D Gaussian Splatting Compression via Two-Stage Optimization
alternate_titles: SpeedyGS: Content-Aware 3D Gaussian Splatting Compression via Two-Stage Optimization
papers.abstract: Recent progress in compressing large-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) data has substantially reduced storage footprint, network transmission bandwidth, and memory traffic to GPU caches before rendering. Yet decoding with advanced 3DGS codecs still takes seconds, making them unsuitable for interactive applications. To systematically address this challenge, we propose SpeedyGS, a Content-Aware 3DGS Compressor that separately optimizes the structural formation and statistical coding. First, in structural formation, we jointly optimize adaptive quantization and pruning under a unified rate-distortion objective, where the rate term is replaced by a lightweight rate proxy that estimates entropy coding cost of the next stage, thereby efficiently regulating Gaussian density and precision to yield a compact scene representation. papers.title: Spectral-Prior Asymmetric Fusion with NLL-Guided Ensemble Learning for EEG–fNIRS Imagined Handwriting Decoding
alternate_titles: Spectral-Prior Asymmetric Fusion with NLL-Guided Ensemble Learning for EEG–fNIRS Imagined Handwriting Decoding
papers.abstract: Imagined handwriting decoding offers a promising pathway toward non-invasive brain-to-text communication without requiring overt speech or physical movement. However, learning reliable neural representations from limited multimodal brain-signal data remains challenging. Existing methods typically rely on convolutional filters to discover task-relevant frequency patterns directly from the data, without explicitly incorporating the characteristic neural oscillations associated with motor imagery. Moreover, conventional symmetric or tightly coupled multimodal fusion may allow less informative fNIRS signals to interfere with the more discriminative EEG pathway. To address these challenges, we propose a unified framework for EEG--fNIRS imagined handwriting decoding. papers.title: Sparse Retrieval Memory with Dynamic Expansion for Class-Incremental Learning
alternate_titles: Sparse Retrieval Memory with Dynamic Expansion for Class-Incremental Learning

However, a critical pre-training bottleneck limits practical adoption. To overcome this bottleneck, we propose Sparse Retrieval Memory, an external sparse memory architecture that can be directly deployed on frozen pre-trained Vision Transformers without architectural surgery or re-pre-training. papers.title: Semantic-Embedded Bitstream: An INR-based Image Compression Framework Supporting Instant Editing
alternate_titles: Semantic-Embedded Bitstream: An INR-based Image Compression Framework Supporting Instant Editing
papers.abstract: Editing compressed images at a semantic level typically requires three heavyweight steps: decoding the bitstream to obtain a reconstructed image, applying computer vision operations such as detection, segmentation, or inpainting in the pixel domain, and re-encoding the result to produce an updated bitstream. This pipeline makes semantic editing computationally expensive and impractical at the decoder side. To address this limitation, we present the first INR-based image compression framework that produces a semantic-embedded bitstream, enabling semantic-level editing directly in the bitstream through only lightweight operations. Object attributes, including color, position, and occlusion, can be modified at will without any decoding, re-encoding, or pixel-domain processing. papers.title: SEROA: Stable Encrypted-Traffic Representation and Online Adaptation for Service-Aware Networks
alternate_titles: SEROA: Stable Encrypted-Traffic Representation and Online Adaptation for Service-Aware Networks
papers.abstract: Mobile networks are evolving toward service-aware operation to support heterogeneous applications with diverse quality-ofservice (QoS) and quality-of-experience (QoE) requirements. In practice, however, the widespread use of encryption makes service types difficult to observe directly, which limits the deployment of service-aware optimization in operational networks. Recent raw-byte representation learning methods have improved offline encrypted-traffic classification, but their robustness in realistic deployment remains limited due to temporal drift and the lack of explicit labels for online adaptation. This paper proposes Stable Encrypted-Traffic Representation and Online Adaptation (SEROA), a deployment-oriented framework for encryptedtraffic classification in service-aware mobile networks. papers.title: SAVeR$^2$: Reasoning-based Safety Alignment for Large Reasoning Models via Verifiable Rewards
alternate_titles: SAVeR$^2$: Reasoning-based Safety Alignment for Large Reasoning Models via Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have achieved impressive performance via explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, yet this process introduces critical safety risks. We formalize LRM safety objectives as requiring non-malicious reasoning and answers, safety consistency, and explicit intent identification. We argue that existing alignment methods suffer from poor adversarial generalization, a significant ``safety tax'' on reasoning, and unfaithful coarse-grained rewards, primarily due to their neglect of the LRM's intrinsic reasoning capabilities for safety. To address these, we propose \textbf{SAVeR$^2$}, a novel \textbf{S}afety \textbf{A}lignment method via \textbf{R}ewards with \textbf{R}easoning capability. alternate_titles: Route-DMD: Distribution Matching Distillation with Task-Routed Mechanism for Speech Foundation Models

We show that a distribution-matching objective does not serve every task: in separation, the noised states of erroneous student outputs deviate far from the teacher's training distribution, where its prediction is unreliable. papers.title: Render Structure Uncertainty for HTML Repair in MLLM-based UI-to-Code Generation
alternate_titles: Render Structure Uncertainty for HTML Repair in MLLM-based UI-to-Code Generation
papers.abstract: Existing MLLM-based UI-to-Code generation methods can generate complete HTML/CSS codes through end-to-end or multi-stage pipelines, yet the generated codes often contain structural errors such as incorrect repeated layouts, wrong component boundaries, or missing interaction slots. Subsequent generations may continue along the erroneous structure, causing the error to propagate and amplify. This paper studies post-generation repair: how can we locate and repair unreliable local DOM structures? We observe that this repair process is ambiguous in two ways: a mismatch between the target screenshot and the output may correspond to multiple plausible DOM subtrees, and a single DOM subtree may admit multiple repairs with different rendered behaviors. papers.title: QRAE: Query-Relevant Attention Entropy for Context Compression in DeepSearch Agents
alternate_titles: QRAE: Query-Relevant Attention Entropy for Context Compression in DeepSearch Agents
papers.abstract: DeepSearch LLM agents repeatedly search and carry retrieved sources into subsequent reasoning steps. This expanding context increases token consumption and latency, although many results do not contribute to later reasoning. We propose Query-Relevant Attention Entropy (QRAE), an online context compression method that uses sparse evidence-assessment heads to decide which intact retrieved chunks should persist across reasoning steps. It scores bounded candidate batches through paired prefills: a query-free control suppresses shared attention responses, while normalized entropy measures the breadth of the positive response within each chunk. High-scoring chunks enter a persistent evidence whitelist and are included in the reasoning context. papers.title: QAQ: Query-based Attack for Query-based Object Detection
alternate_titles: QAQ: Query-based Attack for Query-based Object Detection
papers.abstract: Transformer-based detectors have transformed the detection paradigm by leveraging the concept of object queries and set prediction. This end-to-end paradigm, while simplifying the detection pipeline, also introduces additional adversarial vulnerabilities. alternate_titles: PlayGen2: Learning Real-Time Playable Worlds with Explicit 3D State

papers.title: Pipelining the Memory Hierarchy for Ultra-Long-Context Language Model Training
alternate_titles: Pipelining the Memory Hierarchy for Ultra-Long-Context Language Model Training
papers.abstract: Long-context language models are attractive because they can read whole documents, code repositories, conversations, and scientific sequences. Direct long-context training is blocked by temporary memory spikes from activations, attention buffers, communication workspaces, and the final loss computation, even when model parameters and optimizer states are already sharded. Our proposed method, Fully Pipelined Distributed Transformer (FPDT), treats the long sequence problem as a memory-hierarchy scheduling problem. alternate_titles: Personalized health coaching via coachable health age and counterfactual wearable trajectories

alternate_titles: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Continual Reinforcement Learning (CRL) agents struggle to adapt to new situations while retaining prior knowledge, leading to a stability-plasticity trade-off. Anand & Precup (2023) instantiated this idea using permanent and transient value functions, but used the same features in both systems. Intuitively, long-term learning should rely more on parametric representations for broad generalization, while transient learning would be best served by non-parametric representations for situation-specific adaptation. alternate_titles: NeuroMM 2026: The 1st International Workshop on Multimodal Neurophysiological Intelligence for Multimedia
papers.abstract: Multimedia intelligence primarily models observable content and behavior, yet many human-centered tasks depend on neural and bodily dynamics. alternate_titles: MedVES: Visual Evidence Scaling at Test Time for VLMs in Medical VQA
papers.abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) hold significant promise for clinical image understanding, but scaling them at training time is limited by data privacy constraints and the cost and scarcity of expert annotations. alternate_titles: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained LLM Reasoning for Technique Identification from Malware Reports
papers.abstract: Mapping behavioral intelligence in malware analysis reports to ATT&CK techniques supports threat analysis and defense, but reliable identification remains challenging. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. papers.title: Improving Long-Tail Detection via Layout-Instruction Conditioned Diffusion Synthesis
alternate_titles: Improving Long-Tail Detection via Layout-Instruction Conditioned Diffusion Synthesis
papers.abstract: Synthetic data from diffusion models can improve object detection, but long-tail performance is still limited by scarce rare classes and inflexible conditioning (e.g., text-only or layout-only inputs). In this paper, we propose Tail-SD, a layout-instruction conditioned stable diffusion framework that supports text, layouts, or their hybrid, enabling controllable synthesis from boxes, masks, and/or prompts to better cover the long-tail objects. To train a single model across heterogeneous conditions, we introduce a multi-task cross-attention module and multi-task embedding tokens, improving generation quality and diversity. Extensive experiments on COCO and LVIS demonstrate that diffusion synthesis with hybrid conditioning consistently benefits detection, e.g., on LVIS val, it achieves +4.89% / +5.68% rare Box/Mask AP, highlighting strong potential for addressing long-tail challenges.

papers.abstract: We design adversarially robust algorithms for dynamic geometric streams that $(1 + ε)$-approximate $k$-Median and $k$-Means in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$, using $\tilde{O}(kd \mathrm{poly}(ε^{-1}))$ space. This result significantly improves a recent $O(d\log n)$-approximation for $k$-Median [Gribelyuk, Lin, Woodruff, Yu, and Zhou, FOCS 2026], and is furthermore the first algorithm whose space is linear in $kd$, even in the oblivious (non-adaptive) setting. We develop several new techniques which may be of independent interest, including a new data-oblivious Euclidean primitive called hierarchical Lipschitz assignment, a robust dimensionality reduction for clustering, and a robust streaming algorithm for inner-product queries.

papers.title: A Generative Model of Contextual Integrity: Appropriate vs. Inappropriate Information Sharing
alternate_titles: A Generative Model of Contextual Integrity: Appropriate vs. Inappropriate Information Sharing
papers.abstract: Contextual integrity (CI) holds that appropriate information flow depends on context-specific norms. The same disclosure may be appropriate in one context and inappropriate in another. We build a generative model of contextual integrity to study information sharing through simulated conversations. Two actors played by large language models exchange messages, with one holding private information and the other seeking it. We examine how sharing and refusal vary with the situation, the holder's decision logic, disposition, and the underlying language model. Actors shared information with the rightful recipients when it was needed, but also disclosed it to people who were not entitled to receive it. The model provides a way to study how disclosure and refusal develop through conversation as the situations and the actors vary.

papers.abstract: Domain-specific languages (DSLs) for deep learning, such as Triton, reduce the development effort required to write high-performance GPU kernels. However, debugging Triton kernels remains challenging. To facilitate quick and streamlined debugging, we present TritonParse, a unified framework that systematically collects and organizes debugging evidence to help developers efficiently localize Triton kernel failures. TritonParse follows a 4R workflow: Record, Reconstruct, Review, and Reproduce. Beginning with capturing compilation and launch metadata, TritonParse then reconstructs traces into analyzable forms by aggregating data from multiple sources, supports human-in-the-loop inspection through a user interface, and generates reduced single-kernel reproducers (runnable programs that replay captured kernels) for manual debugging and automated regression analysis. From Handcrafted to Generative: RLVR-Optimized Icon Generation for Alexa+
papers.abstract: Alexa+ devices with screens display animated icons during conversations to visually reinforce what is being said. The original set of these icons was hand-drawn by designers one at a time, a process that produces polished results but is time-consuming and cannot scale to the range of topics encountered in open-ended conversation. We describe an automated pipeline, deployed in production, that generates these vectorised animated icons from a text description alone and surfaces relevant animations to customers based on their ongoing conversation. The pipeline decomposes icon creation into a sequence of stages (image generation, semantic decomposition, vectorisation, styling, and animation). Its quality is determined at the very first of these, image generation, on which every downstream stage depends. We therefore focus on improving this first and most critical stage. papers.title: How to Build Digital Humans? From Priors to Photorealistic Avatars
alternate_titles: How to Build Digital Humans? From Priors to Photorealistic Avatars
papers.abstract: Abstract This state‐of‐the‐art report provides an overview of controllable 3D human avatar creation. We describe current 3D avatar systems, which typically consist of three stages: (i) learning priors of human appearance and motion, (ii) creating a personalized avatar, and (iii) animating the avatar. To limit the scope, we focus on the prior learning and avatar creation stages. We define current avatar representations and introduce a taxonomy that categorizes existing work along multiple axes, including body regions and employed priors. We review methods for full‐body and head avatars, as well as layered representations that decompose the body into components such as hands, hair, and garments. Finally, we outline common underlying principles, reference key literature for newcomers, and discuss open challenges and future research directions.

papers.title: TIRx: A Unified Tile Primitive ML Compiler Across Heterogeneous Backends
alternate_titles: TIRx: A Unified Tile Primitive ML Compiler Across Heterogeneous Backends
papers.abstract: Modern ML kernels evolve rapidly with new optimizations and hardware features. ML compiler abstractions must accommodate richer memory hierarchies, more forms of thread cooperation, and increasingly heterogeneous backends while retaining the control required for peak performance. We present TIRx, an ML compiler for GPUs and AI accelerators that exposes these ingredients through explicit interfaces. TIRx introduces an explicit execution-scope abstraction that captures participating hardware teams at multiple granularities. It also uses tensor layouts to map logical tensors to heterogeneous hardware spaces through named axes and shard/replica/offset semantics. Finally, it introduces tile-primitive dispatch, which lowers high-level operations to efficient implementations according to scope, layout, and backend. papers.title: Consistent Submodular Maximization with Full Foresight
alternate_titles: Consistent Submodular Maximization with Full Foresight
papers.abstract: Online algorithms with bounded recourse face three intertwined obstacles: uncertainty about the future, computational limits, and a limited budget for changes. We ask a fundamental question that separates consistency from the other two: what does solution stability cost when the entire future is known and computation is unlimited? We answer this question for monotone submodular maximization, where an algorithm must maintain a solution of at most $k$ arrived elements, with a constant number of changes per step. We determine the optimal approximation thresholds: $3/4$ for deterministic algorithms and $ξ^\star \approx 0.7942$ for randomized algorithms. For every $\varepsilon>0$, we get within $\varepsilon$ of these thresholds with worst-case recourse polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$, independent of $k$ and the stream length.
