papers.title: Safe and Programmable OS-Level GPU Resource Management with eBPF
alternate_titles: Safe and Programmable OS-Level GPU Resource Management with eBPF
papers.abstract: GPU resource management policies govern how a system places memory and schedules GPU tasks. They play an important role in determining application performance, and the ideal policy for a given deployment often depends on low-level details such as the application, workloads, and hardware. AI agents would make it possible to automatically optimize GPU resource management policies, but require three properties of a system: safety, to ensure that a broken policy cannot cause a system crash; dynamism, to enable policy changes without restarts; and full-stack, to ensure that the policy can observe device and application states and control low-level hardware. Unfortunately, existing techniques for GPU resource management fail to meet these needs. papers.title: SVGFaith: A Two-Layer Meta-Evaluation of Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation
alternate_titles: SVGFaith: A Two-Layer Meta-Evaluation of Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation
papers.abstract: Text-to-SVG systems are commonly evaluated by applying raster-image metrics to rasterised outputs, yet whether these scores capture fine-grained prompt faithfulness remains unclear. We introduce SVGFaith, a two-layer meta-evaluation framework in which the more faithful candidate of each pair is determined by construction or by human judgment. SVGFaith-Diagnostic contains 1,842 controlled contrastive pairs across eight capability axes, split evenly between two directions: two renderings compared against one prompt, and two descriptions compared against one rendering. SVGFaith-Arena contains 1,327 human-annotated comparisons of real generator outputs. On SVGFaith-Diagnostic, CLIP and three other image--text embedding metrics reach at least 0.789 pairwise accuracy on object identity but at most 0.672 on spatial relations and attribute binding, where chance is 0.5. papers.title: Ruby-OPD: Enhancing Pronunciation Controllability and Accuracy for Flow-Matching Text-to-Speech via On-Policy Distillation
alternate_titles: Ruby-OPD: Enhancing Pronunciation Controllability and Accuracy for Flow-Matching Text-to-Speech via On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Achieving both high pronunciation accuracy and fine-grained controllability remains a central challenge in Japanese text-to-speech (TTS), as Japanese is an unsegmented language mixing logographic Kanji and phonographic Kana with extensive polyphony. Traditional cascaded systems convert text into phoneme sequences via a front-end, ensuring pronunciation control but discarding lexical semantics and prosodic cues in surface orthography. Conversely, recent zero-shot TTS models directly consume raw orthographic text to improve naturalness, yet suffer from polyphone errors and lack explicit pronunciation control. To bridge this gap, we propose a two-stage framework for flow-matching TTS. First, we investigate Ruby text representations with orthography perturbation to jointly preserve surface forms and target pronunciations for reliable control. papers.title: Reward Budgeting Reduces Premature Convergence in Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
alternate_titles: Reward Budgeting Reduces Premature Convergence in Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: RL for LLM reasoning often plateaus early as its policy sharpens. Policy entropy is studied as both a diagnostic and a control signal, but increasing it alone does not reliably change the eventual plateau in our experiments. We analyze RL's implicit target policy using a sharpness factor $κ$ and effective counterpart $κ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ that describe how reward or advantage gaps translate into probability-ratio gaps. We introduce reward budgeting, a plug-in advantage construction assigning a fixed total reward budget to each prompt. For binary rewards and independent on-policy rollouts, its expected unclipped score-function update is the exact gradient of a finite-$G$ concave objective with diminishing returns; its advantage gap decreases as more rollouts become correct. papers.title: Prism: Bidirectional Self-Teaching for Unified Multimodal Models
alternate_titles: Prism: Bidirectional Self-Teaching for Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single model. Existing post-training methods either use understanding as a fixed teacher to improve generation, or rely on ground-truth trajectories to supervise both understanding and generation. Prism instead derives bidirectional supervision from self-generated interleaved rollouts, constructing training targets according to the reliability of their text and image chains. We propose Prism, a bidirectional self-teaching post-training method for UMMs. Like a prism decomposing mixed light, Prism decouples a coupled interleaved trajectory into a text chain and an image chain, assesses the reliability of each chain, and constructs a corresponding training target from their reliability states. papers.title: Practical Estimation of the Bayes Optimal Fairness-Accuracy Tradeoff with Soft Labels
alternate_titles: Practical Estimation of the Bayes Optimal Fairness-Accuracy Tradeoff with Soft Labels
papers.abstract: There is a fundamental limit to the best prediction error of any model for a given data distribution. In classification, the Bayes error quantifies this limit and serves as both a benchmark for trained models and a criterion to detect overfitting. The state-of-the-art Bayes error estimation techniques for binary classification use only soft labels (positive class probabilities) and require no input features or auxiliary training. We extend such notions to constrained classification problems, such as fairness. Fair classification is an important case of constrained or multi-objective classification. It requires a model not only to be accurate but also to yield fair outcomes (equal or near-equal true positive rates) across different demographic groups (e.g., race and gender). papers.title: MicrobeRT: A Framework and Suite of Fine-tuned Language Models for Genomic Sequences
alternate_titles: MicrobeRT: A Framework and Suite of Fine-tuned Language Models for Genomic Sequences
papers.abstract: Accurate and reproducible metagenomic analysis is essential for effective infectious disease surveillance. Targeted diagnostics such as culturing, antigen assays, and multiplex PCR panels identify only predefined organisms and can fail to identify atypical or novel infections. Shotgun metagenomics offers hypothesis-free detection, but adoption is limited by workflow complexity, dependence on mutable reference databases, and high computational cost. To combat these challenges, we introduce MicrobeRT, an integrated suite of genomic language models fine-tuned to classify metagenomic sequencing reads across three tasks: (i) species level taxonomic identification, (ii) antibiotic resistance gene detection, and (iii) pathogenicity assessment. papers.title: Measuring Risk, Not Harm: Detecting Psychological Harm Risk Factors in LLM Conversations
alternate_titles: Measuring Risk, Not Harm: Detecting Psychological Harm Risk Factors in LLM Conversations
papers.abstract: Psychological harms from interactions with large language models cannot be monitored directly because they may emerge over repeated interactions and depend strongly on subjective individual user context. We propose measuring risk, not harm: detecting observable AI behaviors that constitute risk factors for psychological harm at the AI response level and aggregating these signals to support longitudinal monitoring. We operationalize eight such behaviors and construct a synthetic multi-label corpus of 47,062 AI responses and 373,873 response-factor labels, with targeted human annotations for validation and evaluation. We then compare trained embedding-based classifiers, direct LLM judging, and a classifier--judge cascade. papers.title: LiveFoley: Dynamic Real-Time Video-to-Audio Generation for Immersive Interactive Worlds
alternate_titles: LiveFoley: Dynamic Real-Time Video-to-Audio Generation for Immersive Interactive Worlds
papers.abstract: Streaming video-to-audio (V2A) generation is essential for immersive interactive applications. However, real-time constraints leave existing streaming V2A methods far behind offline models: (1) visual frontends shrink their receptive fields to cut look-ahead latency, severely degrading audio-visual alignment; (2) causal autoregressive diffusion backends denoise each audio patch in isolation, impairing audio quality. To this end, we present LiveFoley, a streaming causal autoregressive diffusion architecture that addresses both bottlenecks with imperceptible latency. For the visual frontend, we introduce a Trailing Sliding Window that converts non-causal segment-level encoders into streaming modules without retraining. papers.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
alternate_titles: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: The performance of large language model (LLM) agents depends on both the underlying model and the harness that governs interaction with tools and the environment. Yet harness design remains largely manual, and automating it requires navigating an open-ended search space through costly end-to-end evaluations. We introduce HarnessFlow, a framework for optimizing complete executable harnesses under a limited candidate-evaluation budget, with the model and task environment held fixed. HarnessFlow organizes candidates and their evaluation histories in a refinement tree, using a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based policy to balance exploitation and exploration. A coding agent refines selected harnesses using archived code, execution feedback, and a library of reusable harness mechanisms. papers.title: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles
alternate_titles: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles
papers.abstract: Recent LLM-centric advances can generate attractive furnished rooms by selecting and arranging assets. Yet evaluation remains limited to specific perspectives or predefined questions, failing to reflect overall scene quality. To address this pressing need, we introduce GREP. Its core is a focus shift from defining specific questions to establishing a three-tier evaluation philosophy: basic physical validity checks whether a scene obeys physical constraints; visual coherence concerns compatibility in object scale, style, and composition; and, at the highest level, human-use logic requires object arrangements to align with everyday human habits. alternate_titles: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
papers.abstract: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics, FrontierPhysics evaluates whether agents' research is correct and publishable. alternate_titles: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices
papers.abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. papers.title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
alternate_titles: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
papers.abstract: Generative video models are increasingly used as visual world simulators, yet their primary strength lies in rendering plausible pixels rather than reasoning about how a world should evolve. Coherent world evolution requires more than visual fidelity: when an event occurs, a model must infer its consequences for the entities in the world and then render the resulting state. For example, after a wild beast appears, the model should not only depict the wild beast, but also infer whether a nearby person should flee, take cover, or fight back based on the realized scene. Existing diffusion-based video models lack an explicit mechanism for maintaining world state and reasoning over such event-conditioned consequences, often producing visually plausible but behaviorally static or causally inconsistent outputs. papers.title: Evaluating Human-LLM Alignment on Visualization Preference
alternate_titles: Evaluating Human-LLM Alignment on Visualization Preference
papers.abstract: There are often multiple valid visualizations, spanning different chart types, visual encodings, and aesthetic choices, that can all support a user's goal of analyzing a dataset. Determining which of these candidate visualizations is most appropriate, however, remains challenging. Prior work has leveraged expert-curated taxonomies to guide visualization design and subsequent quality evaluation, a practical evaluation model must also account for human-centric factors. Latest visualization tools integrate Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and refine visualizations, using LLM-as-a-judge to provide design feedback. Without a deeper understanding of whether, and in what ways, human and LLM perceptions of visualizations align, there is a real risk of deploying low-quality agents that do not reflect human judgment. alternate_titles: Entropogram-guided Visual Realignment Decoding: Capturing the Rhythm of Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress on cross-modal reasoning tasks, yet they continue to suffer from hallucinations in long-chain reasoning processes. In this work, we revisit hallucination in MLLMs from the perspective of reasoning generation dynamics. We argue that entropy is not merely a static measure of uncertainty but a structured signal that reflects how modality information is integrated throughout decoding. Through systematic analysis, we identify two characteristic entropy patterns associated with hallucination behaviors: (1) a generally high-confidence regime corresponds to premature convergence to inappropriate multimodal interactions; and (2) local abrupt entropy transitions are associated with reasoning instability and hallucination onset. alternate_titles: EDIVA: Exploiting Human Behavioral Patterns for Differential Egocentric Video Processing in AR
papers.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) systems increasingly rely on real-time image segmentation to interpret continuous egocentric video streams and enable immersive, intention-aware interactions. However, executing neural segmentation models on every high-resolution frame introduces significant computational overhead and latency, exceeding the real-time constraints of AR devices. This paper presents EDIVA, an algorithm–hardware co-optimization framework for differential egocentric video processing that exploits temporal redundancy and multimodal sensory cues in AR environments. EDIVA uses gaze, pose, and inertial signals to infer user intent and reproject previous segmentation masks via perspective transformation, updating only regions with significant visual changes. alternate_titles: Do Search-Augmented Recommenders Use the Latest Search Episode?
papers.abstract: Search-augmented recommenders can use the latest search episode and earlier searches. We introduce FocalSwap to test how these inputs contribute to the next recommendation. For each recommendation, it changes the latest search slot or all search inputs while holding the target, candidates, pre-search history, and scorer fixed. It compares neutral masks with matched observed-search replacements, recording rank changes, RR gains relative to each control, and preference for the true focal search. A planted signal and GenSAR's current-query task confirm that the audit detects known input dependence. papers.title: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models
alternate_titles: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Time series forecasting is critical for demand prediction and resource management in modern Web services, yet applying pretrained Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) to downstream tasks remains challenging due to domain shifts. Existing retrieval-augmented approaches typically retrieve coarse-grained window contexts and may introduce context-specific noise. To address this problem, we argue that temporal patterns should be reused at a decomposition level, as effective trend and seasonal dynamics may originate from different contexts. alternate_titles: Chronos: Sequential Identity-Preserving Video Generation by Temporal Anchoring
papers.abstract: Identity-preserving video generation aims to synthesize high-quality and visually realistic videos from textual and visual conditions while faithfully maintaining the subject's identity across diverse motions. However, improving static identity alignment alone creates a fundamental tension between identity fidelity and temporal controllability, which frequently causes identity drift or motion suppression under large pose variations and multi-segment sequential actions. To address this, we propose Chronos, a framework that unifies single-segment facial identity preservation and multi-segment sequential action generation under a common temporal formulation. alternate_titles: CRESiST: Self-Enhancing Explorative Policy Learning for Simultaneous Speech Translation
papers.abstract: Simultaneous Speech Translation (SimulST) requires balancing translation quality and latency. While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in offline translation, current LLM-based SimulST systems predominantly rely on prefix-incremental generation. This paradigm suffers from redundant Key-Value cache recomputation and necessitates external Voice Activity Detection to process unbounded streams. To overcome these bottlenecks, we propose an end-to-end interleaved read-write framework built upon an omni-modal LLM. By interleaving speech chunks and text tokens, our architecture achieves full KV cache reuse, natively supporting segmentation-free, infinite-length inference. papers.title: Beyond the Landing Page: Website Blocking, Tracker Visibility, and Human Alignment in Automated Web Crawls
alternate_titles: Beyond the Landing Page: Website Blocking, Tracker Visibility, and Human Alignment in Automated Web Crawls
papers.abstract: Web tracking studies largely rely on automated crawlers, yet their measurements can differ from what people encounter while browsing. Conventional crawlers follow predefined navigation rules, whereas LLM-driven agents decide how to navigate and interact with websites, potentially changing the tracking they encounter. We compare agentic and non-agentic crawlers to examine how websites respond to them, what tracking they record, and how closely their observations match human browsing. Across 2,000 popular websites, we evaluate different navigation strategies, automation frameworks, and stealth configurations, alongside browsing data from 26 participants. papers.title: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI
alternate_titles: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI
papers.abstract: Current generative AI alignment relies on a myopic paradigm that prioritizes immediate conversational satisfaction. By relying on short-horizon feedback, this approach ignores the profound, longitudinal externalities of persistent human-AI interaction, which can lead to adverse outcomes such as cognitive atrophy, social erosion, and diminished human agency. To address this, we propose a paradigm shift toward long-horizon alignment that accounts for how AI reshapes human experience over time. To this end, we map the tensions between near-term utility and long-term costs of AI use across four facets of human well-being to reveal outcomes that current reward models fail to capture. Ultimately, we advocate for moving beyond simple preference optimization toward alignment strategies that actively foster long-term human well-being by navigating these complex temporal scales.

papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding assistants and agents construct a repository context before generating code. However, context construction is designed almost exclusively for functional correctness, and secure-code benchmarks treat the context as fixed, so how repository context affects the security of generated code remains unclear. Each task runs in Docker, has functional tests and a proof-of-concept exploit validated in both directions, and is annotated with the repository code that enforces or undermines its security. alternate_titles: $D^2$-OPD: Separating Direction and Distance in Extrapolative On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model to match a teacher's next-token distributions on student-generated prefixes. Extrapolative OPD further extends the teacher's log-probability shift relative to a reference policy to construct stronger learning targets. However, existing methods couple extrapolation direction and distance, allowing the magnitude of the teacher's shift to dictate how far the target moves. We propose $D^2$-OPD, decoupling these two factors: a per-prefix hard KL constraint bounds the target's distance from the teacher, while an adaptive combination of the teacher's post-training shift and the initial student--teacher gap determines the extrapolation direction. We optimize the student toward this target using forward KL, providing learning signals even for low-probability tokens. alternate_titles: Systolic Linear Attention: Co-Designing Tile-Grouped Gated Delta Attention for TPUs
papers.abstract: Gated-delta linear attention layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), and GDN-2 are tuned for GPUs, where small tensor-core tiles and fast vector registers make per-channel decay rescaling and sequential in-block solves cheap. On Google TPUs, which concentrate compute in wide $256 \times 256$ systolic matrix units backed by a slower vector unit, porting these layers directly leaves half of each matrix tile empty and bottlenecks on vector operations. papers.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
alternate_titles: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. Some approaches rely on human teleoperation and wearable capture devices, which require at least an hour of human time to produce an hour of data. We present HALO, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes. alternate_titles: GRAIL 2026: Workshop on Generative, Retrieval-augmented, and Agentic Intelligence for Personalization
papers.abstract: Personalization is being rebuilt around generative models. Large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and agentic systems now shape how recommenders retrieve, rank, explain, converse, and even simulate users—yet they also surface hard problems of hallucination, control, evaluation, privacy, and fairness. GRAIL 2026 brings together academic researchers and industry practitioners to advance generative, retrieval-augmented, and agentic approaches to recommendation—including LLM-based retrieval and ranking, retrieval-augmented and knowledge-grounded personalization, conversational and agentic recommenders, multimodal content generation, user simulation, and synthetic data—while giving equal attention to these open challenges and their long-term user impact.

However, vulnerabilities reported in real-world systems show that prompt injections vary widely. Ignoring this variation leaves gaps in how defenses are evaluated, and can give a false sense of security against real-world attacks. We identify nine dimensions along which prompt injection attacks differ. Together, they form a taxonomy that describes the injected instruction itself, its relation to the user's task, and how it manifests in the target system. Each dimension affects which defenses can detect or prevent an attack. We first use the taxonomy to characterize six real-world prompt injection vulnerabilities, showing how much th...

papers.title: Temporal Moment Generation: A New Recommendation Task and Cost-Efficient Distillation for Outbound Marketing at Scale
alternate_titles: Temporal Moment Generation: A New Recommendation Task and Cost-Efficient Distillation for Outbound Marketing at Scale
papers.abstract: Outbound marketing at scale relies on content-first programs and item-ranking pipelines that match a fixed catalog to recent activity, missing the long-horizon interests and seasonal context (e.g., back-to-school, Earth Day) that make a message relevant. Missing these signals has played a key role in engagement declines of up to 18% year-over-year, with 55% of push notifications rated irrelevant by users. We make two contributions. First, we formalize temporal moment generation as a new recommendation task, distinct from item ranking: rather than scoring a catalog against a customer, the system starts from why a specific customer should be reached now. Given a customer behavioral signal profile and reference time T, it generates temporally-grounded moments---each a name, trigger, bounded activation window, and message hook, plus tiered search phrases for product retrieval---feeding a dow...

papers.title: TTSonic: A Unified Framework for Composable and Controllable Speech Generation
alternate_titles: TTSonic: A Unified Framework for Composable and Controllable Speech Generation
papers.abstract: Modern text-to-speech (TTS) systems can synthesize natural and expressive speech, yet a practical speech foundation model must go beyond naturalness to offer stable quality, precise controllability, and a broad set of composable capabilities within a unified framework. We present TTSonic, a unified speech generation model that supports zero-shot TTS, voice cloning, prosody cloning, instruction following, voice conversion, and cloning from noisy reference speech. Rather than relying on separate task-specific models, TTSonic accommodates diverse conditioning signals, including text, natural language instructions, reference speech, and text-described timbre, within the same model framework. Specifically, we develop a semantic--acoustic disentangled speech tokenizer through ASR-supervised semantic learning and reconstruction-guided generative refinement. Serving as the representational found...

papers.title: TACT: A Pragmatic Approach to Qualitative Analysis with an AI Council
alternate_titles: TACT: A Pragmatic Approach to Qualitative Analysis with an AI Council
papers.abstract: Qualitative data can tell software teams what their stakeholders need, yet rigorously analyzing thousands of qualitative responses takes expert time that few teams can afford or justify. Teams therefore often face a false choice: leave the responses unanalyzed, or hand them to a large language model and accept its interpretation and judgment. In this paper, we take a pragmatic approach to AI-assisted qualitative analysis and present TACT (Traceable AI Council for Thematic analysis), a procedure that enables such analysis at scale while keeping teams in control of interpretation and judgment. TACT comes in two variants: TACT-Lite, the core AI council procedure, and TACT-Full, which adds adversaries (models from other model families that critique each model's output) and a decision model that surfaces high-uncertainty code assignments. We evaluated TACT on an independent dataset of 256 Sta...

papers.title: T-MSDF: T-shaped Convolutional Multi-stream Discovery Framework with LLM-Driven Compatibility Priors
alternate_titles: T-MSDF: T-shaped Convolutional Multi-stream Discovery Framework with LLM-Driven Compatibility Priors
papers.abstract: In modern recommender systems, the ''filter bubble'' effect remains a formidable challenge as models tend to over-exploit historical interactions at the expense of potential interest discovery. Although various exploration strategies have been proposed, effectively balancing prediction precision with serendipity within the ranking layer remains an open problem. To address this challenge, this paper introduces T-MSDF , a novel T-shaped convolutional Multi-stream Sequential Discovery Framework. T-MSDF leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to construct a category affinity table that quantifies semantic complementarity between product categories, enabling the generation of augmented behavior sequences along exploration paths grounded in real-world common-sense logic. The framework consists of four synergistic components: (1) an LLM-constrained Sequence Expansion module that generates knowle...

papers.title: Support-Adaptive Complexity Control for Longitudinal Counterfactual Prediction
alternate_titles: Support-Adaptive Complexity Control for Longitudinal Counterfactual Prediction
papers.abstract: Longitudinal counterfactual prediction aims to forecast future outcomes under candidate treatment sequences from observational trajectories. Existing methods mainly address time-varying confounding and temporal representation learning. We identify a complementary finite-sample challenge: counterfactual queries often lie in history-action regions with highly heterogeneous logged support. This leads to the support-complexity mismatch for the fixed-capacity prediction heads used by existing methods. Motivated by finite-sample learning theory, where reliable generalization depends on function-class complexity relative to the number of relevant samples, we propose Support-Adaptive Complexity Control (SACC) to address this issue, a backbone-agnostic method that replaces the fixed action-conditioned prediction head with a support-adaptive one. SACC estimates rollout-conditioned local support fo...

papers.title: SourceFlow: Collaborative Source Coupling for Flow-Based Recommendation
alternate_titles: SourceFlow: Collaborative Source Coupling for Flow-Based Recommendation
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based recommenders learn user preferences by denoising interaction histories, but the added noise can distort the original preference signals. Flow-based collaborative filtering (CF) instead learns a discrete path from a sampled source to the user's observed training interactions (the target history), enabling inference in a few steps. Existing flow-based CF methods sample sources using global item frequencies to reflect the sparsity and popularity of observed interactions. Each source is sampled independently of its target history, leaving the predictor without user-specific source cues for learning to reconstruct that history. We propose SourceFlow, which brings collaborative structure into the source distribution itself rather than adding further conditioning to the predictor. Like inference from observed histories, training uses collaborative evidence to predict missing int...

papers.title: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Evaluating Web Agents Against Online Fraud
alternate_titles: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Evaluating Web Agents Against Online Fraud
papers.abstract: Web agents increasingly browse, shop, and manage accounts on behalf of their users. Prior work has shown that they can be misled by adversarial content, including prompt injections and deceptive interfaces. Beyond such attacks, agents operating on the open web also encounter online fraud designed to deceive humans, including fraudulent online stores, fake investment platforms, and advance-fee schemes. How web agents respond to such fraud during task execution remains underexplored, in part because scam websites are short-lived, making systematic evaluation difficult. To address this gap, we introduce ScamWorld, an interactive environment that reconstructs reported scam websites across diverse scenarios, fraud mechanisms, and languages. Each reconstructed website reproduces documented fraud mechanisms, making relevant signs of fraud observable before the agent's final action and enabling...

papers.title: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents
alternate_titles: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: The memory of production agents is increasingly becoming a bottleneck and is built almost exclusively from text: key points are extracted from out-of-limit context and retrieved into context at query time. Therefore, every new query incurs an additional cost that grows with the accumulated history. Weight memory is a complementary alternative that internalizes knowledge into model parameters and answers with no context at all, and has recently proven effective in self-evolving agents for internalizing skills and behaviors. However, its application in episodic and semantic memory, such as user-specific facts, remains comparatively unexplored, and a gap remains between earlier attempts at weight memory and text-based systems regarding recall performance. We study how to make weight memory competitive as a long-term factual store by applying on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). It trains a c...

papers.title: ReuseGR: Offline--Online Decoupled Generative Retrieval via Adaptive Prefix Reuse
alternate_titles: ReuseGR: Offline--Online Decoupled Generative Retrieval via Adaptive Prefix Reuse
papers.abstract: Larger generative retrieval models can improve retrieval quality, but their decoding cost makes low-latency serving difficult. When different users submit the same query, generating complete Semantic IDs (SIDs) for every request repeats computation, while their interaction histories call for different results. The challenge is to reuse large-model computation across requests while keeping retrieval personalized. We propose \textbf{ReuseGR}, which separates query-level candidate planning from request-level personalized completion. A 7B offline planner generates SID prefix sets shared across requests with the same query. A 0.5B online model uses each request's history to select prefixes and generate the remaining tokens. ReuseCut chooses a cache depth for each query based on historical coverage, balancing computation reuse and candidate coverage. To strengthen online completion, we transfe...

papers.title: Reliability Stress Testing of RAG Retrieval under Query-Relevant Corpus Poisoning
alternate_titles: Reliability Stress Testing of RAG Retrieval under Query-Relevant Corpus Poisoning
papers.abstract: External text can affect a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system only after the retriever admits it to the model context. We stress this admission step while varying document content, attacker query information, per-target poison budget, and contamination scope. Across 623 Benchmarking Information Retrieval (BEIR) queries from SciFact and NFCorpus, five query-targeted documents per query reduce classical-retriever nDCG@10 by 40.2-61.5% in isolated-target stress. Full-query anchoring explains most Best Matching 25 (BM25) degradation, whereas appended text also shifts latent semantic analysis (LSA) and Hybrid rankings. papers.title: Rebuilding the Content Ranking Stack for Prime Video: Lessons Learned Building from Scratch
alternate_titles: Rebuilding the Content Ranking Stack for Prime Video: Lessons Learned Building from Scratch
papers.abstract: We present the rebuild of Prime Video's Response Predictor (RP), the ranking stage of its recommendation system, replacing a foundation model next-item predictor with a Deep Interest Network that scores a title conditioned on context at request time. The surrounding data, feature, training, and serving stack was developed natively and validated through online experimentation. This paper concentrates on the system rather than the model and presents three lessons from building it at scale. First, label design influences business outcomes more strongly than model architecture. Second, the feature store, as the core infrastructure, must reconstruct serving-time features both correctly and efficiently at training scale. Third, offline metrics are an unreliable guide to production impact, and continuous online measurement and monitoring proved essential to identifying what improved business ou...

papers.title: REACH-AI 2026: Community-Informed Evaluation and Benchmarking of Culturally Competent Generative AI
alternate_titles: REACH-AI 2026: Community-Informed Evaluation and Benchmarking of Culturally Competent Generative AI
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Generative AI (GenAI) have enabled strong capabilities in language understanding, content generation, vision-language reasoning, and multimodal interaction. However, most existing benchmarks emphasize general-purpose reasoning and task performance, offering limited evaluation of whether AI systems can accurately understand, represent, retrieve, and generate culturally grounded knowledge across diverse communities and social contexts. This limitation restricts the reliable deployment of GenAI in high-impact domains such as education, healthcare, and public services. The REACH-AI 2026 Workshop brings together researchers, industry leaders, practitioners, and community stakeholders to advance community-informed approaches for evaluating culturally competent Generative AI. Motivated by the REACH GenAI Consortium, a collaboration between Google Research and twelve Historica...

papers.title: RAFT: Reasoning-Aligned Fine-Tuning Improves Robustness of VLA Post-Training
alternate_titles: RAFT: Reasoning-Aligned Fine-Tuning Improves Robustness of VLA Post-Training
papers.abstract: Adapting a generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a target task with limited demonstrations can improve nominal task success while reducing robustness to variations in appearance, objects, and instructions. We introduce reasoning-aligned fine-tuning (RAFT), a two-stage post-training procedure: RAFT first trains low-rank adapters on task-relevant reasoning annotations, then freezes them while fine-tuning the policy on action demonstrations. On a physical DROID robot, RAFT achieves $75.0\%$ out-of-distribution success, compared with $27.9\%$ for plain fine-tuning; on a multi-stage bimanual YAM task, it reaches $70.0\%$ mean success, compared with $36.0\%$ for the strongest baseline. RAFT also improves success under visual, object, and instruction shifts in simulated pick-and-place and open-drawer tasks. Compared with plain fine-tuning, RAFT policies place more attention on annot...

papers.title: Prompt‐Aware Graph Reasoning and Explicit Ranking for Multi‐Trait Essay Scoring in Intelligent Education
alternate_titles: Prompt‐Aware Graph Reasoning and Explicit Ranking for Multi‐Trait Essay Scoring in Intelligent Education
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Automated essay scoring (AES) plays a critical role in providing rapid and objective feedback in language assessment. However, cross‐prompt multi‐trait scoring faces two primary challenges: modelling complex topological dependencies between writing dimensions and overcoming the regression paradigm's fragility against feature shifts on unseen prompts, which often leads to blurred boundaries in fine‐grained. Current approaches frequently overlook these cognitive inter‐dependencies and fail to capture subtle cross‐essay discrepancies. To address these limitations, we propose Prompt‐Aware Graph Reasoning and Explicit Ranking (PAGER). Specifically, a decoupled feature extraction mechanism utilising a stop‐gradient strategy is first deployed to mitigate overfitting and prevent representation collapse. We then employ a prior‐guided sparse topology coupled with a dynamic semantic gating...

papers.title: Process In-Context Learning: Confusion-Aware Demonstration Retrieval and Dynamic Insertion for Mathematical Reasoning
alternate_titles: Process In-Context Learning: Confusion-Aware Demonstration Retrieval and Dynamic Insertion for Mathematical Reasoning
papers.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) has achieved strong results across a wide range of large language model (LLM) tasks. However, its effectiveness for problems that require step-by-step deduction, such as mathematical reasoning, is still not well understood. One major limitation of existing ICL methods is that demonstrations are chosen before inference and remain unchanged throughout reasoning. As a result, they cannot respond to confusion points that emerge during multi-step problem solving, such as uncertain calculations or missing logical transitions. When these confusion points are not resolved, they may propagate and ultimately degrade answer accuracy. To address this limitation, we propose Process In-Context Learning (PICL), a dynamic demonstration insertion framework for mathematical reasoning. PICL consists of two stages: 1) it identifies potential confusion points by analyzing semantics...

papers.title: Privacy-Aware Representation Decoupling in Federated Recommendation against Attribute Inference Attacks
alternate_titles: Privacy-Aware Representation Decoupling in Federated Recommendation against Attribute Inference Attacks
papers.abstract: Federated recommender systems (FedRec) aim to preserve user privacy by keeping sensitive data on client devices and sharing only model parameters with a central server. However, FedRec is still vulnerable to attribute inference attacks (AIAs), where server-side adversaries exploit uploaded parameters to infer users' private attributes. Existing FedRec approaches face a suboptimal privacy-performance trade-off. Privacy-focused methods mask attribute-related features in representations to protect sensitive information, but degrade recommendation accuracy. In contrast, performance-focused methods preserve accuracy by retaining these features but risk privacy leakage through uploaded representations. To balance privacy and performance, we propose PARD, a privacy-aware representation decoupling framework that explicitly decomposes representations into privacy-relevant and privacy-irrelevant c...

papers.title: Positional Encoding is All You Need for Scalable Equivariance Constraint Relaxation
alternate_titles: Positional Encoding is All You Need for Scalable Equivariance Constraint Relaxation
papers.abstract: Equivariant neural networks incorporate known symmetries of the data, such as permutations, rotations, or translations, directly into their architecture, often improving sample efficiency and generalization. However, strict equivariance can make optimization difficult, for example, when the data only approximately satisfy the assumed symmetry, or when the equivariance constraints induce a challenging loss landscape. Recent studies have shown that relaxing equivariance during training by introducing non-equivariant dense linear layers can ease optimization in such cases and improve the performance of the resulting strictly equivariant model, after removing the relaxation layers at test time. While effective, this approach incurs a significant computational overhead, limiting its applicability in scalable architectures. In this work, we propose a more efficient constraint-relaxation method...

papers.title: Pay Where It Matters: Accurate and Versatile Bit-Level Stream Analytics with Nino-Sketch
alternate_titles: Pay Where It Matters: Accurate and Versatile Bit-Level Stream Analytics with Nino-Sketch
papers.abstract: Analyzing high-velocity data streams is critical for tasks like real-time monitoring, anomaly detection, and performance analysis, driving interest in sketches, probabilistic data structures that efficiently summarize fast streams. Traditional sketches often use large, fixed-size counters, leading to inefficient memory usage in skewed data distributions. Recent solutions, such as hierarchical structures and dynamic counters, attempt to improve memory efficiency but struggle to balance this with detection accuracy. In this work, we present Nino-Sketch, a memory-efficient and versatile sketch for data stream analysis. Nino-Sketch employs a flexible filter to exclude cold items (e.g., those with low frequency or persistence) while focusing on tracking hot items using variable-size counters. papers.title: Pairing Expert Critique with LLM-Driven Refinement: An Iterative Approach for Curating Quality AI Evaluation Datasets
alternate_titles: Pairing Expert Critique with LLM-Driven Refinement: An Iterative Approach for Curating Quality AI Evaluation Datasets
papers.abstract: Evaluating and improving domain-specific LLM responses requires high-quality reference data and rubrics, yet expert authoring is slow and expensive, and synthetic datasets may fail to capture practitioner preferences unless they are grounded in expert judgment. We present SME-C (Subject Matter Expert Critique), a human-AI workflow that captures expertise through lightweight critiques of candidate responses and complements it with LLM-driven analysis and refinement to iteratively curate response datasets and evaluation rubrics. We validate SME-C in the domain of financial business briefs, collecting 3,853 critiques from 411 finance professionals on 520 queries across two survey rounds. We evaluate two LLM-driven refinement strategies: one guided by the experts' written critiques and one that infers critique solely from their preference votes. In a blind validation survey with 100 addition...

papers.title: PATTS: Parallel-Aware Test-Time Scaling for Thought-Image Generation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion LLMs
alternate_titles: PATTS: Parallel-Aware Test-Time Scaling for Thought-Image Generation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion LLMs
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves generative models by allocating additional inference-time computation to sampling, search, and verification. Existing image generation approaches, however, typically rank completed images or image-centric intermediate states. We study TTS for parallel multimodal discrete diffusion language models, in which reasoning tokens and image tokens are decoded jointly within a single generation trajectory. We first diagnose a limitation of conventional final-image selection: on GenEval, a CLIP-style image-prompt score is weakly aligned with within-prompt compositional correctness, leaving substantial headroom between verifier selection and oracle selection. We then propose PATTS, a novel parallel-aware TTS framework that searches over intermediate thought-image states using cross-modal verifier signals. PATTS uses a state-dependent reliability weight, derived from...

papers.title: OGX: An Open-Source, Vendor-Neutral Generative AI Application Server
alternate_titles: OGX: An Open-Source, Vendor-Neutral Generative AI Application Server

papers.title: OCR in the Foundation Model Era: From Specialist Models to Unified Models
alternate_titles: OCR in the Foundation Model Era: From Specialist Models to Unified Models
papers.abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is among the oldest and most widely deployed applications of artificial intelligence. This survey reviews its development, focusing on the Foundation Model Era. We define OCR through faithful transcription: within a specified visual scope, OCR should completely reconstruct the text, notation, and document structure observable in the source image, and every textual, notational, or structural element in the output must be verifiable from visual evidence in that image. We trace the development from specialist OCR models toward unified models, examining joint text detection and recognition, structured sequence generation, and the use of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs). We organize contemporary OCR systems into five coexisting families: modular toolkits and task-specific models, specialized document VLMs, hybrid workflows, general-purpose VLMs, and...

papers.title: Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)
alternate_titles: Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)
papers.abstract: Existing work on Semantic IDs (SIDs) for generative recommendation treats SID construction as a representation learning problem: encode items into a quantised latent space and read off codes. We argue this view is incidental. SID construction is, at heart, a recursive clustering problem, and once stated this way the natural object to cluster is a graph whose nodes carry semantic content and whose edges carry collaborative signal; SID assignment becomes a hierarchical graph partition. This reframing yields a unified framework, Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS), that subsumes prior approaches rather than displacing them. RQ-VAE and RQ-KMeans are recovered as the special case where the graph is empty, exposing content-only quantisation as one corner of a larger design space along two so-far-collapsed axes: graph construction and recursive partition algorithm. We explore two contrasting ins...

papers.title: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation
alternate_titles: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation
papers.abstract: We aim to build a truly unified motion model that can understand, generate, and edit human motion within a single framework. Existing motion UMMs remain only partially unified: motion understanding is handled by a language model, while generation is often delegated to a separate diffusion module operating over learned motion latents. We introduce Möbius, which brings the entire diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for motion understanding. Clean motion, noisy motion, and text jointly participate in shared attention, while role-specific parameters process understanding and generation streams. Importantly, Möbius operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion, requiring neither discrete tokenization nor a pretrained motion VAE. This simple formulation naturally supports motion captioning, text-to-motion generation, temporal completion, and instructio...

papers.title: Machine learning emulators of dynamic global vegetation models for fast gridded carbon budget predictions
alternate_titles: Machine learning emulators of dynamic global vegetation models for fast gridded carbon budget predictions
papers.abstract: The land carbon sink explains most of the variability of the atmospheric CO2 growth rate, but the Global Carbon Budget estimates it with dynamic global vegetation models (DGVMs) run once a year. Emulators could provide it sooner if they reproduce each model outside its training period. Here we show that convolutional neural network emulators of 19 of these models, driven by ERA5 climate and their own past predictions, reproduce the global land sink of these models and its spread over two years not used in training. Global monthly net biome production (NBP) anomalies were reproduced with a median R^2 of 0.81. The error of the multi-model mean annual NBP was at most 0.23 GtC yr^-1. At the grid-cell level, the median R^2 of monthly anomalies was 0.30, partly because of errors that accumulate in the emulated NBP history.

papers.title: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games
alternate_titles: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games
papers.abstract: We study repeated general games over $T$ rounds between a utility-maximizing optimizer and a learning agent, where budget constraints couple the players' decisions across rounds. Without budgets, low swap regret simultaneously guarantees the learner sublinear regret and caps the optimizer at its Stackelberg value. Budgets break this picture: adversarial no-regret becomes impossible, so the natural goals are non-manipulability---no adaptive optimizer earns more than $\mathtt{BSE} \cdot T + o(T)$, where $\mathtt{BSE}$ is its Budgeted Stackelberg Equilibrium value---and low stochastic regret when the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy. papers.title: Learning to Design Information
alternate_titles: Learning to Design Information
papers.abstract: Information designers, such as large language models and online platforms, often do not know the subjective beliefs of their receivers or users. We construct learning algorithms enabling the designer to learn the belief of a strategic receiver through repeated interactions. Our learning algorithms are robust to the receiver's strategic manipulation of the learning process of the designer. We study regret relative to two benchmarks to measure the performance of the algorithms. The static benchmark is $T$ times the single-period optimum for the designer under a known belief. The dynamic benchmark, which is stronger, characterizes global dynamic optimality for the designer under a known belief. Our learning algorithms allow the designer to achieve no regret against both benchmarks at fast convergence speeds of $O(\frac{\log^2 T}{T})$, significantly faster than other approaches in the litera...

papers.title: Learning from What You Retrieve: Online RL Fine-Tuning for Semantic Retrieval
alternate_titles: Learning from What You Retrieve: Online RL Fine-Tuning for Semantic Retrieval
papers.abstract: In large-scale e-commerce retrieval, dual-encoder retrievers are optimized for contrastive similarity, whereas downstream rerankers capture finer-grained relevance preferences; this objective mismatch limits end-to-end retrieval quality. Reinforcement Learning offers a way to use reward-model feedback for retriever adaptation, but we observe that standard policy-gradient updates can degrade embedding geometry, especially when the document index must remain frozen due to industrial constraints. To address this, we propose PAO (Positive-Advantage-Only) , a selective RL optimization method. Our analysis reveals that indiscriminate penalization of negative samples (pushing away) in a frozen high-dimensional space disrupts pre-trained semantic manifolds. papers.title: Learning Where to Look: Observation Policy Optimization for Thinking with Images
alternate_titles: Learning Where to Look: Observation Policy Optimization for Thinking with Images
papers.abstract: Complex visual question answering often requires vision-language models to think with images, i.e., actively acquire local visual evidence by zooming into informative regions of high-resolution images. Our error analysis shows that many failures in this setting originate from incorrect observation actions, where the model fails to localize key regions or obtain crops that contain sufficient evidence for answering. We further observe that bounding-box tokens exhibit substantially higher generation entropy than ordinary language tokens, indicating high uncertainty when the model decides where to look. However, existing reinforcement learning methods based on final-answer rewards provide only trajectory-level feedback, making it difficult to assign precise credit to the observation actions. We propose Observation Policy Optimization (OPO), an RL algorithm for optimizing observation actions...

papers.title: LLMJudge: Meta-Evaluating Automatic Relevance Judgments
alternate_titles: LLMJudge: Meta-Evaluating Automatic Relevance Judgments
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to produce the relevance labels that underpin the evaluation of information retrieval (IR) and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Yet delegating relevance assessment to an LLM raises a meta-evaluation question that is hard to answer with existing resources: when, and how much, can we trust an automatic judge? We present LLMJudge, a resource for meta-evaluating LLM-generated relevance judgments. LLMJudge collects 42 complete judgment sets over the TREC 2023 Deep Learning track, spanning fine-tuned, proprietary, and open-source models and a wide range of prompting strategies. Each judgment set is paired with official human qrels, enabling two complementary axes of analysis: label agreement with human assessors (e.g., Cohen's κ, Krippendorff's α) and system-ranking fidelity (e.g., Kendall's τ, Spearman's ρ). papers.title: LIFT: A Learning-aware Intervention Framework for Cold-Start Recommendation on TikTok Live
alternate_titles: LIFT: A Learning-aware Intervention Framework for Cold-Start Recommendation on TikTok Live
papers.abstract: On billion-scale live streaming platforms such as TikTok, a core challenge is to distribute millions of newly initiated live streams to potential viewers. The ephemerality and real-time variability of live streams demand an aggressive and dynamic cold-start strategy to capture value within an extremely limited window. Beyond this temporal urgency, the system faces a unique challenge: a two-way interactive feedback loop in which recommendations directly influence streamer behavior and subsequent viewer feedback. Traditional methods, however, lack the ability to intervene at critical learning moments and fail to provide the active incentives needed to optimize the streamer-user feedback loop. In this paper, we propose LIFT (Learning-aware Intervention Framework for Cold-Start Recommendation on TikTok Live), a novel paradigm designed specifically for this real-time intervention. LIFT employ...

papers.title: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
alternate_titles: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Probabilistic time-series forecasting requires models that simultaneously capture structured temporal dynamics, expressive uncertainty, and efficient inference, yet existing approaches fall short of this goal: latent dynamical models impose structure but rely on restrictive generation mechanisms, while modern generative methods such as diffusion and flow matching achieve flexibility at the cost of iterative and computationally expensive sampling. papers.title: Knowledge Graphs Data Quality at Scale: Challenges, Solutions, and Applications
alternate_titles: Knowledge Graphs Data Quality at Scale: Challenges, Solutions, and Applications
papers.abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are foundational infrastructure for search, question answering, and entity-centric applications, on the open web and within domain-specific platforms. Their lifecycle, from construction over heterogeneous sources to evaluation at scale and use in downstream tasks, raises a coupled set of data management problems that shape the reliability and utility of every system built on top of them. This tutorial offers a high-level view of KG data quality at scale, organized along KG lifecycle stages. We first frame KG construction and the open challenges that arise when facts are extracted from noisy, evolving sources. We then turn to evaluation, covering efficient quality estimation, as well as the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) as validators and auxiliary signals. papers.title: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models
alternate_titles: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) integrate image generation and visual understanding, but are existing single-pathway unlearning methods sufficient to suppress target concepts across both? In this work, we study cross-pathway concept unlearning. Our goal is to prevent a model from both generating images of a target concept and identifying it in input images, while preserving other capabilities. To this end, we introduce UUBench, a diagnostic benchmark covering 30 target concepts and 60 semantically related neighboring concepts. Experiments on representative UMMs show that the evaluated single-pathway methods achieve limited joint forgetting: generation-side editors strongly suppress target generation but yield limited forgetting in visual understanding, while understanding-side baselines struggle to achieve substantial forgetting even in their own pathway. papers.title: IDs That Mean Something: A Hands-On Tutorial on Semantic IDs for Recommender Systems
alternate_titles: IDs That Mean Something: A Hands-On Tutorial on Semantic IDs for Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Traditional recommender systems rely on arbitrary integer IDs to identify items, which carry no semantic information and force models to learn representations from interaction data. While leveraging content information can partially mitigate cold-start, this paradigm inherently suffers from exploding embedding tables and scenario-specific architectures. Recent years have seen the emergence of semantic IDs, which encode semantic information directly into the item identity, reflecting content, hierarchy, and relationships. This framework addresses the above limitations by offering a principled way to encode large-scale semantic information into item identity, benefiting both generative and discriminative applications and unlocking more native unification across modalities, domains, and tasks. This tutorial traces the evolution from raw IDs to semantic IDs as a scalable means of information...

papers.title: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing-in-Ground-Effect Dataset for Benchmarking Neural Surrogate Models
alternate_titles: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing-in-Ground-Effect Dataset for Benchmarking Neural Surrogate Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents a CFD dataset of a highly parametrized 3D wing operating in ground effect, designed for benchmarking neural surrogate models for aerodynamic prediction, using a wing shape and flow conditions typically encountered in motorsport applications. The dataset comprises 770 RANS simulations of 194 unique wing configurations, sampled across 27 airfoil profile variants and 4 distances from the ground, spanning variations in wing sweep, chord, taper, angle of attack, and tip twist. Six neural network architectures representing distinct paradigms --- convolutional (DoMINO), graph-based (X-MeshGraphNet), transformer-based (AB-UPT, GeoTransolver, GAOT), and JEPA-based (AeroJEPA) --- are evaluated on their ability to predict surface pressure coefficient and wall shear stress distributions, from which integral drag and lift coefficients are recovered. papers.title: GRID: Generative Recommendation via Inpainting Diffusion
alternate_titles: GRID: Generative Recommendation via Inpainting Diffusion
papers.abstract: Generative Recommendation (GR) utilizing discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) has emerged as a promising paradigm for sequential recommendation. However, existing GR paradigms exhibit significant generation flaws: traditional autoregressive (AR) models suffer from strict left-to-right causal constraints leading to error accumulation, while current discrete diffusion adaptations rely on isolated next-item beam search, which causes ''homogeneous stacking'' and lacks explicit list-level coordination. Furthermore, these methods often compromise the interpretable, hierarchical structure of SIDs. To address these limitations, we propose GRID, a novel framework that reformulates generative top-K recommendation as a 2D discrete diffusion inpainting problem. By modeling the recommended item list and their multi-digit hierarchical SIDs along two orthogonal axes, GRID recovers the complete matrix of future...

papers.title: FreeForm Harness: A Mobile-Native Agent Harness for Open and Composable Extensions
alternate_titles: FreeForm Harness: A Mobile-Native Agent Harness for Open and Composable Extensions
papers.abstract: Mobile phones support many everyday agent tasks, but current mobile agents bundle capabilities into monolithic pipelines with no open recombination point. Users and third parties cannot publish, install, and compose new behaviors, leaving personalized daily-life requests underserved. We argue that the missing piece is a substrate: although phones are the Web's dominant access point, open publication and composition under decentralized authorship stop at the agent harness. We present FreeForm Harness (FFH), a mobile-native agent harness for open, composable extensions. A frozen base and a permanence-aware required layer handle mobile constraints, including location, proactive triggering, and scarce channels. A uniform plugin contract makes independently authored extensions composable, checkable, and replaceable over a frozen socket set. FFH also supports end-user authorship through a tier...

papers.title: Files Search Relevance using Wide and Deep Networks
alternate_titles: Files Search Relevance using Wide and Deep Networks
papers.abstract: Unlike web-search, enterprise search queries are more contextual, documents are private and heterogeneous, and ground-truth relevance labels are scarce. Production systems at this scale have long relied on gradient-boosted decision tree (GBDT) models such as LightGBM with hand-engineered features, given their speed, interpretability, and robustness on numeric features. However, high-quality semantic embeddings from large, pre-trained language models open new possibilities for neural learning-to-rank models that can jointly learn from sparse hand-crafted features (e.g., personalization signals such as user activity, document recency, and lexical matching features like BM25) and dense semantic representations. In this paper, we present our work on using wide & deep neural networks for search relevance over the enterprise files data. Due to privacy constraints on customer data, which limits...

papers.title: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models
alternate_titles: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Post-training updates change what large language models (LLMs) can answer, but may leave their answerability judgments misaligned. We study this knowledge-judgment desynchronization through functional feeling of knowing (FoK), which supports selective generation, retrieval triggering, and model routing without implying subjective experience. We propose two trainable channels: a knowledge channel that changes answerability and a FoK channel that judges the current knowledge state. Three stages train them: on-policy supervised fine-tuning (OP-SFT) updates knowledge from corrected on-policy answers; knowledge-delta FoK training (K$Δ$-FT) adapts judgments across intermediate knowledge states; and FoK-guided policy optimization (FGPO) trains the subsequent answer or explanation. papers.title: FailSafe-RAG: Evidence-State-Aware Generation under Retrieval Failures
alternate_titles: FailSafe-RAG: Evidence-State-Aware Generation under Retrieval Failures
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves factual grounding by conditioning language models on retrieved evidence, but its reliability depends on whether the retrieved list is relevant, consistent, and semantically grounded. When retrieval fails under coverage gaps, conflicting passages, or lexical matching traps, generators may still produce definitive but unsupported answers. We propose FailSafe-RAG, a lightweight and training-free framework that treats retrieval failure as an explicit post-retrieval evidence state. Inspired by Query Performance Prediction (QPP) and retrieval-list coherence analysis, FailSafe-RAG estimates three evidence-risk indicators: coverage insufficiency, conflict risk, and evidence noise. A risk-prioritized policy maps the resulting risk state to behavior-conditioned generation, enabling clarification, abstention, cautious answering, or direct assertion with...

papers.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
alternate_titles: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
papers.abstract: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text. Although recent approaches leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown significant progress, we argue that the MLLM's compositional understanding remains underutilized. This stems from directly mapping composed queries into a retrieval embedding via contrastive supervision alone, without explicitly resolving the intended visual modifications. In this work, we introduce Factorized MLLM Embeddings (FactEmbed), which decouples compositional query comprehension from building discriminative embeddings. Rather than directly projecting the composed query into a single embedding without internal reasoning, FactEmbed employs a set of factorized latents that simulate the intended visual modifications via an intermediate target imagination objective. papers.title: FAF: A Feature-Aware Adaptive Pre-training Framework for Bridging Gaps in CTR Prediction
alternate_titles: FAF: A Feature-Aware Adaptive Pre-training Framework for Bridging Gaps in CTR Prediction
papers.abstract: Self-supervised pre-training has emerged as an effective solution to data sparsity in Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction. However, existing paradigms still face two critical limitations: (1) task degeneration in pre-training, where heuristic or random target construction may lead to trivial shortcuts; and (2) limited adaptivity in fine-tuning, where static transfer strategies fail to accommodate optimization heterogeneity across diverse feature fields and ID frequencies. To address these issues, we propose the Feature-aware Adaptive pre-training and fine-tuning Framework (FAF). The core of FAF lies in two coupled designs. First, we improve pre-training target construction from both token and feature levels. papers.title: ExPert infers causal perturbations from cell states across biological and clinical contexts
alternate_titles: ExPert infers causal perturbations from cell states across biological and clinical contexts
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Pooled single-cell CRISPR screens have driven substantial effort toward models predicting the response to a perturbation. We posed the inverse question: which perturbation produced an observed cell state? Here we developed ExPert (Extracting Perturbations), which learns one prototype per perturbation in a latent space shared by 12 cellular contexts, trained on 8,964 perturbations and 19.5 million cells, and ranks 19,895 candidate genes per query, over half absent from training. ExPert more than doubled held-out-context recall over the best existing method with 1,000-fold less compute, and transferred without retraining to drugs, protein degradation and combinations. papers.title: Efficient and Faithful High-Resolution Image Editing with Sparse Cross-Resolution Denoising
alternate_titles: Efficient and Faithful High-Resolution Image Editing with Sparse Cross-Resolution Denoising
papers.abstract: Instruction-based image editors still primarily operate at 1K, whereas practical editing increasingly requires faithful 2K/4K outputs. Dense high-resolution adaptation preserves the editing trajectory but incurs expensive target-source attention; editing at 1K followed by external refinement is cheaper but can separate detail restoration from the editing trajectory. We introduce FLASH, a native high-resolution editor based on sparse cross-resolution denoising. A frozen 1K branch provides a semantic and structural anchor, while a target-resolution branch reconstructs local detail within the same Transformer. An asymmetric topology retains full 1K attention, guides high-resolution queries with spatially aligned low-resolution noisy-target states, and confines high-resolution target-reference interaction to local Halo neighborhoods. papers.title: Efficient Frame Selection for E-Commerce Video Analysis
alternate_titles: Efficient Frame Selection for E-Commerce Video Analysis
papers.abstract: E-commerce video analysis systems---spanning fulfillment-center (FC) packaging and return-center (RC) unpackaging---face two challenges at scale: transferring and indexing full-resolution video is prohibitively expensive (evidence collection), and downstream Vision Language Model (VLM) inference requires query-specific evidence frames (evidence analysis). We propose a two-stage frame selection approach: Stage 1 is a query-agnostic on-device video summarizer that compresses each video to k keyframes via Determinantal Point Process diversity and Laplacian-variance quality scoring (8× reduction, ?1% of frames transmitted); Stage 2 is a set of domain-adapted per-category relevance rankers fine-tuned with a pairwise RankNet loss on human-verified labels. papers.title: EP-LVMQA: Evidence-Preserving Coarse-to-Fine Localization for Low-Quality Long Video Moment Question Answering
alternate_titles: EP-LVMQA: Evidence-Preserving Coarse-to-Fine Localization for Low-Quality Long Video Moment Question Answering
papers.abstract: Long instructional videos are increasingly used in medical education, industrial training, and procedural knowledge transfer, yet their evidence is often incomplete or unreliable: subtitles may be missing, ASR noisy, OCR sparse, and decisive actions briefly shown without narration. Existing VideoQA systems typically return labels or free-form text, making answer support difficult to inspect. We study Long Video Moment Question Answering (LVMQA), where a system returns timestamped answer-supporting evidence. We propose EP-LVMQA, an evidence-preserving coarse-to-fine framework comprising an Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Evidence Timeline, a Coarse Evidence Planner, and an Evidence-Conditioned Fine Localizer. An evidence card transfers planner scores, matched cues, source-confidence proxies, modality-specific evidence, neighboring context, and a temporal prior between the latter two modules....

papers.title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation
alternate_titles: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation
papers.abstract: LLM-based recommender systems increasingly generate chain-of-thought (CoT) text before each item prediction to activate the LLM's reasoning capacity, costing tens to hundreds of extra tokens per recommendation at inference. We ask whether inference-time reasoning artifacts (textual or latent) can be replaced by training-time supervision alone, without loss of accuracy. We propose LatentRec, a framework for LLM-based generative recommendation that replaces inference-time reasoning artifacts with training-time per-step head supervision. LatentRec has three components. A 2.5M-parameter Continuous Thought Module iterates K latent reasoning steps over the LLM's hidden state during training. papers.title: Do Multi-Turn Conversational Capabilities Carry Over from Text to Speech? A Parallel Multilingual Benchmark
alternate_titles: Do Multi-Turn Conversational Capabilities Carry Over from Text to Speech? A Parallel Multilingual Benchmark
papers.abstract: Successful multi-turn voice interaction requires models to retain information from earlier turns, follow persistent instructions, and track revisions to conversational state. These abilities are usually evaluated from transcripts, leaving open whether successes demonstrated from text carry over when the same turns are spoken, and whether this transfer is consistent across languages. We introduce Omnilingua-AudioMC, a strictly parallel multilingual extension of Audio MultiChallenge, to study this question. The benchmark contains 354 conversations and 1,404 rubric items across ten languages, with content, turn structure, cross-turn dependencies, and evaluation criteria aligned across transcript and speech conditions. papers.title: Discarded or Unreachable? Diagnosing and Repairing Spatial Relation Failure in Vision--Language Similarity
alternate_titles: Discarded or Unreachable? Diagnosing and Repairing Spatial Relation Failure in Vision--Language Similarity
papers.abstract: Contrastive vision-language models score left/right relations near chance, but the symptom has two causes that call for opposite repairs: the relation may survive in the pooled embedding yet be unreachable by native image-text similarity, or pooling may discard it while the dense features retain it. On clean two object photographs, across ten encoders, the lateral polarity is linearly decodable from the flip odd component of the pooled vector at 0.77-0.99, yet a search over a million captions leaves nine of the ten at chance under native scoring: an access failure. On controlled C4 orbits, where the relation is the only thing that varies, pooling keeps the arrangement axis at 0.998-1.000 and loses its polarity, which the patch grid retains: a pooling failure. papers.title: Diagnosis by Composition: Detecting and Localizing Unseen Diseases by Composing Learned Radiological Findings
alternate_titles: Diagnosis by Composition: Detecting and Localizing Unseen Diseases by Composing Learned Radiological Findings
papers.abstract: Deep models for radiological diagnosis are typically trained to predict disease labels directly from images, which limits them to diseases seen during training and makes their decisions hard to interpret in radiologists' terms. Radiology, however, proceeds from visual findings to disease through published guidelines that make this decision rule explicit, interpretable, and reproducible. We introduce diagnosis by composition (DbC), a representation learning framework that encodes this findings-first logic. DbC learns a vocabulary of radiological findings by aligning image features with the text embeddings of the findings, each finding represented as a dense map over the scan. A disease is defined by a set of required findings derived from its guidelines, and its diagnosis map is a fixed, parameter-free composition of the corresponding finding maps.
