papers.title: Decision Models as Scalable Economic Surrogates that Capture Human Variation
alternate_titles: Decision Models as Scalable Economic Surrogates that Capture Human Variation
papers.abstract: Decision Models (DMs), a new class of AI models, give fast responses and return a probability distribution over a fixed set of options. These properties make them candidate human surrogates in economic simulations and surveys, a role increasingly filled by Large Language Models (LLMs), which are costly at scale and under-represent the variation in human behaviour. We present a first evaluation of DMs as human surrogates in economics, comparing 10 DMs with 8 LLMs in three economic settings: a household spending survey on consumption, several classic economic games and a labour-market field experiment. Frontier DMs, those that score highest on general decision-making benchmarks, reproduce the variation in human responses more closely than LLMs in all three settings. papers.title: DataDescribe: Auto-Generated Source Descriptors for LLM-Agent Retrieval over Heterogeneous Data
alternate_titles: DataDescribe: Auto-Generated Source Descriptors for LLM-Agent Retrieval over Heterogeneous Data
papers.abstract: LLM agents over heterogeneous external data—databases, document collections, APIs—must decide which sources to load into a finite context before retrieval. Query-side embedding routing misses source-level properties (topic specialization, density, freshness); unifying all sources into one dense index dilutes retrieval and pays the per-engine retrieval cost across the entire federation. We introduce DataDescribe, a describe-then-decide method that auto-generates a compact six-facet descriptor per source (schema, size, variety, entropy, temporal density, freshness) once at ingestion and exposes it to plug-in source selectors composed with federated retrieval. papers.title: DGC-Net: Cross-Modal Dynamic Routing with Global-Guided Compensation in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
alternate_titles: DGC-Net: Cross-Modal Dynamic Routing with Global-Guided Compensation in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
papers.abstract: User-generated videos, including opinion vlogs and video reviews, provide a rich source of people's attitudes toward products, services, and social topics. Understanding the sentiment expressed by speakers is important for analyzing online opinions, as transcripts alone may not capture the attitude and intensity conveyed through vocal tone and facial expressions. Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) addresses this need by integrating textual, acoustic, and visual cues. However, these cues are often subtle, noisy, and inconsistent across modalities. Existing local affective cue modeling methods typically operate within individual modalities and overlook global contexts from other modalities. This may cause cross-modal affective cue inconsistency. Hierarchical global-local fusion methods integrate global semantics with fine-grained local affective cues. papers.title: Controllable Autoregressive Retrieval with Long-term Action Perception for Recommendations
alternate_titles: Controllable Autoregressive Retrieval with Long-term Action Perception for Recommendations
papers.abstract: Autoregressive retrieval (AR) has emerged as a leading paradigm for the first stage of industrial recommender systems. However, existing AR methods (i) overlook long-term action perception, training their generation only against the immediate next interaction, and (ii) lack the controllability needed to align candidate generation with diverse business goals without retraining. We propose Controllable Autoregressive Retrieval with long-term action perception (CAR), a simple yet deployable framework that addresses both issues. A long-term supervision module attaches multiple action-sliding prediction heads at different future horizons and transfers their knowledge to the main model via parameter sharing (P-CAR) or cascading (C-CAR), injecting a long-horizon perspective. papers.title: Cognitive Bias Signatures in Search-Equipped LLM Agents: A Stage-Resolved Analysis
alternate_titles: Cognitive Bias Signatures in Search-Equipped LLM Agents: A Stage-Resolved Analysis
papers.abstract: Search can help LLM agents correct mistakes, but their starting conditions may shape which evidence they find and use. Drawing on cognitive-bias paradigms, we develop a controlled search harness to examine result order, records of prior work, and initial hypotheses while holding each question and document collection fixed. Matched controls distinguish order effects from differences in document composition and the effects of failed work from context length. Across 10 models and 1,000 synthetic search worlds, we track queries, retrieved documents, document openings, and final answers. Our comparisons suggest that final answers are more sensitive to initial evidence order during active search than when all evidence is supplied in full. papers.title: ClusterRec: Cluster-Aware Recommendation with Large Language Models for Efficient and Scalable Inference
alternate_titles: ClusterRec: Cluster-Aware Recommendation with Large Language Models for Efficient and Scalable Inference
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have significantly improved recommender systems by enabling richer semantic modeling of user preferences. However, existing LLM-based recommenders typically require expensive per-user inference over long interaction sequences, causing computational costs to scale rapidly with both model size and the number of users. To address this challenge, we propose ClusterRec, a framework that decouples LLM-based recommendation into two stages: (1) group-level preference modeling and (2) user-level personalization. Specifically, users are first clustered based on behavioral representations, and LLMs are employed to construct a group-level semantic representation for each cluster. papers.title: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning
alternate_titles: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Generating HTML from natural-language specifications is an important application of code large language models (LLMs). Despite producing renderable pages, current models often fail to ensure functionality and visual quality during actual interaction. Existing methods typically target task-specific webpage supervision, leaving demanding interactive artifact optimization underexplored. Using mini-games as a challenging testbed, we expose limitations in interaction experience, reward signal, and credit assignment fidelity that are obscured by shallow webpage interactions. We introduce WebCatalyst, a browser-interaction reinforcement learning framework with three complementary components: a game-level GUI assessor for sustained interaction and evaluation, Visual Anchor for mitigating VLM reward hacking, and Action-Trace Credit for grounding token-level credit assignment in runtime execution...

papers.title: Bridging Queries and Brands: Entity Linking for Large-Scale Product Search
alternate_titles: Bridging Queries and Brands: Entity Linking for Large-Scale Product Search
papers.abstract: Associating user search queries with the correct brand entity is critical for e-commerce product retrieval, yet remains challenging due to the brevity of queries (three to four words on average), their lack of grammatical structure, and a catalog of hundreds of thousands of distinct brands. We formulate this as a brand entity linking task and develop two complementary solutions deployed at scale: (1) a cascaded pipeline that first detects brand mentions via sequence labeling and then disambiguates against a brand knowledge base, and (2) a single-stage approach that frames linking as extreme multi-class classification, directly mapping queries to brand identifiers. papers.title: Bidirectional Centered Score Matching for Discrete Diffusion Distillation
alternate_titles: Bidirectional Centered Score Matching for Discrete Diffusion Distillation
papers.abstract: Discrete diffusion models with parallel decoding are often distilled using token-wise KL objectives. Although token-wise KL exactly matches the corresponding product-form block distributions, its probability-space optimization geometry and teacher-only candidate truncation may provide insufficient supervision under aggressive few-step distillation. Concrete Score Matching (CSM) provides an alternative within-position objective by aligning relative logit geometry, but its complete pairwise form incurs \mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}|^2) complexity. We propose Bidirectional Centered Score Matching (BCSM), an efficient within-position distillation objective that constructs an \mathcal{O}(K) bidirectional active set, reduces pairwise comparisons to \mathcal{O}(K^2), and factorizes them into an \mathcal{O}(K) objective. papers.title: Beyond Independent Predictions: Learning the Browsing Journey for Sequence-Level Re-ranking
alternate_titles: Beyond Independent Predictions: Learning the Browsing Journey for Sequence-Level Re-ranking
papers.abstract: Re-ranking aims to present users with an ordered list that maximizes sequence-level utility. Industrial deployments widely adopt the Generator--Evaluator framework, where the generator proposes candidate sequences, and the evaluator scores them to select the best one for display. The fidelity of the evaluator's utility estimates thus directly governs recommendation quality. However, existing evaluators predominantly follow the Independent Behavior Modeling (IBM) paradigm, which simplifies the continuous user browsing journey into independent per-item predictions (e.g., CTR). This oversimplification ignores two physical realities: (i) a click can occur only after the item has been reached and impressed, and (ii) items compete for finite user attention. papers.title: Beyond Exposure: Dynamic Income-Fair Ranking under Time-Varying Provider Value
alternate_titles: Beyond Exposure: Dynamic Income-Fair Ranking under Time-Varying Provider Value
papers.abstract: Ranking systems in web search and recommendation must balance relevance-based effectiveness with fairness for item providers. Exposure Fairness seeks to allocate position-induced attention according to item merit, but exposure is only an intermediate signal whose conversion into provider utility varies with context. We therefore define income as the context-dependent provider utility induced by exposure. We formalize Income Fairness, which requires cumulative provider income to be proportional to relevance, and develop a corresponding metric based on a context-dependent unit-income function. We propose DIDRF (Dynamic-Income-Derivative-aware Ranking Fairness), which exploits the quadratic structure of income-fairness violations to derive a prefix-aware, state-calibrated scoring rule that balances effectiveness and income fairness. papers.title: Beyond End-to-End: A Low-Latency, Retrieval-Augmented Chain-of-Thought for Scalable and Explainable Industrial Recommendation
alternate_titles: Beyond End-to-End: A Low-Latency, Retrieval-Augmented Chain-of-Thought for Scalable and Explainable Industrial Recommendation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can provide semantic reasoning for recommendation, but direct LLM invocation is incompatible with the latency, stability, and reliability requirements of industrial ranking systems. We propose RA-CoT (Retrieval-Augmented Chain-of-Thought), a deployment-oriented framework that uses LLM-derived structured reasoning without replacing the production CTR/CVR backbone or placing LLM inference on the blocking serving path. RA-CoT asynchronously generates schema-constrained CoT-derived representations from pre-impression behavior summaries, caches them with validity checks, and falls back to the backbone when no valid reasoning vector is available. Valid reasoning is injected through an availability-aware gated residual module as bounded logit-space compensation, making the LLM signal reusable, safely ignorable, and compatible with millisecond-level serving. papers.title: Auxiliary Focal Discrimination for Recommendation
alternate_titles: Auxiliary Focal Discrimination for Recommendation
papers.abstract: Scaling up recommender models has become a major route to improving recommendation performance, but effective scaling relies on learning robust and discriminative representations. We identify local representation collapse as a critical bottleneck in this process: under sparse feedback, label-distinct samples can be mapped to highly overlapping local neighborhoods, making fine-grained discrimination increasingly difficult. Existing studies of representation collapse mainly focus on global representation statistics, while auxiliary ranking objectives typically apply pairwise supervision broadly across samples, overlooking the localized nature and varying severity of collapse. papers.title: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention
alternate_titles: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention
papers.abstract: Web systems infer user preferences from behavior, ratings, text, and LLM-generated profiles, yet explaining a proxy may reveal its measurement process rather than the preference of interest. We develop an audit framework distinguishing point identification, partial identification, and abstention relative to an explicit reference distribution. Under feature-dependent, arbitrarily signed proxy bias, a strict majority of uncontaminated proxy attributions lets the coordinatewise median recover latent-attribution support and direction and, with externally justified positive scales, magnitude. papers.title: Ask to Be Sure: Informative Interactions for Confident Multi-Turn LLM Recommendation
alternate_titles: Ask to Be Sure: Informative Interactions for Confident Multi-Turn LLM Recommendation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled their use as conversational recommender systems (CRS), demonstrating strong recommendation accuracy and natural dialogue. However, guiding multi-turn interactions to elicit user preferences effectively remains challenging. Existing approaches either use separate reinforcement learning agents with templated interactions or optimize for interactivity judged by another LLM, without measuring how much useful information is actually gained. We propose a new approach that quantifies the effectiveness of each interaction by the reduction in the assistant's uncertainty, measured via entropy over recommendations. papers.title: Anytime-Valid Multi-Objective Online Experimentation with Contrast Certificates
alternate_titles: Anytime-Valid Multi-Objective Online Experimentation with Contrast Certificates
papers.abstract: Large-scale search and recommendation systems routinely run online experiments for ranking models, feed policies, user-interface treatments, and ad/recommendation blending strategies. These launches are rarely single-metric decisions: teams often need to improve click-through rate, conversion, dwell time, retention, or revenue while controlling negative feedback and latency. We propose AV-MO-SOPTIMA++, an anytime-valid framework for multi-objective online experimentation under adaptive traffic allocation and optional stopping. Instead of relying only on marginal arm-objective confidence sequences, AV-MO-SOPTIMA++ uses prospective two-sample contrast confidence sequences for decision-relevant arm pairs; these contrasts may be pre-activated for a fixed decision mode or activated online when new bottleneck constraints appear. papers.title: Amplified and Emergent Safety Risks in Multi-Agent Recommendation and Retrieval
alternate_titles: Amplified and Emergent Safety Risks in Multi-Agent Recommendation and Retrieval
papers.abstract: Recommendation and retrieval systems are increasingly built by composition, with pipelines of LLM-powered agents that retrieve, reason, and act replacing standalone models. This shift inherits long-standing risks while introducing new ones, yet the resulting threats to robustness and safety, and the strategies to contain them, remain underexplored. Focusing on multi-agent recommender systems, this tutorial organises these threats along three tiers, from drift through misalignment to compromise, and separates risks that composition merely amplifies from those that emerge only once agents interact. papers.abstract: Background: In rectal cancer (RC), tumor deposits (TDs) are clinically important as they are associated with a negative impact on prognosis and affect risk stratification as well as management plans. MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. papers.abstract: Online payment platforms generate massive transaction streams that contain rich behavioral signals for financial risk assessment. However, building a transaction foundation model for such tasks faces three major challenges. First, risk signals exhibit multi-scale temporal semantics, spanning immediate intents at the transaction level, short-term rhythms at the daily level, and long-term cycles at the monthly level. Second, financial transactions are inherently noisy and bursty. Third, an inherent objective gap exists between self-supervised reconstruction pre-training and downstream discriminative risk classification, often leading to inefficient adaptation and even negative transfer. papers.abstract: We prove a broad learning-theoretic generalization of the celebrated hardcore lemma concerning the average-case complexity of computing a Boolean function (Impagliazzo, 1995). Here, we study the problem of {retrodiction}, inferring past values of a series, in the context of chaotic dynamic systems. papers.abstract: Spatial audio conveys not only what sounds are present, but where they originate and how they interact with the environment. Recent audio-language models increasingly understand and reason about such scenes, yet spatial audio understanding, generation, and editing remain largely separate. We present Spatial Transfusion, a unified first-order ambisonics (FOA) framework that extends a pretrained spatial audio understanding model to generation and editing through flow matching over VAE latents. We formulate editing as a structured scene transformation over a taxonomy of atomic edits. Keeping the pretrained backbone frozen, we introduce modality-based LoRA routing and a curriculum that progressively adds generation, editing, and natural-language interaction. Experiments show that Spatial Transfusion largely preserves spatial understanding while outperforming full fine-tuning in generation an...

papers.title: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
alternate_titles: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
papers.abstract: Most parameters of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model belong to its experts, and standard training keeps every expert gradient in GPU memory until the optimizer step. This memory grows with the number and size of the experts, so it rises as MoE models scale. We introduce Sonar-MoE, which updates each expert tensor during the backward pass and frees its gradient right away. It brings optimizer-in-backward from dense models to batched MoE expert tensors, so the GPU never holds more than one layer of expert gradients. When we fine-tune OLMoE-1B-7B and Granite-3.1-3B-A800M in bf16 with two expert-kernel backends, Sonar-MoE lowers peak memory by 19% to 22%. Its updates are bitwise identical to standard training without expert gradient clipping, and held-out loss stays within 0.003 of all baselines. Each step also takes 17% to 23% less time than standard training with global-norm clipping. Updat...

papers.title: Self-Evolving Laboratories Through Persistent Digital and Physical Adaptation
alternate_titles: Self-Evolving Laboratories Through Persistent Digital and Physical Adaptation
papers.abstract: Turning a scientific idea into an experiment often requires researchers to build, configure and repeatedly adapt the laboratory around it. This work demands resources and specialized expertise that can place ambitious experiments beyond reach. Here we introduce a self-evolving laboratory framework that connects computation, physical experiments and AI models through persistent cycles of observation and revision. GPT Astra uses camera observations and physical feedback to adapt robotic actions, digital twins and CAD designs. These changes are retained as reusable skills and infrastructure, allowing the laboratory to develop alongside its scientific tasks. In a fume-hood prototype, GPT Astra identified the need for a beaker holder and storage stand and generated successive designs for on-demand 3D printing. Four holder generations and two stand generations culminated in parts integrated in...

papers.title: Seeing Through the Illusion: Test-Time Scaling for World Action Models
alternate_titles: Seeing Through the Illusion: Test-Time Scaling for World Action Models
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) jointly generate actions and imagined futures, but a plausible prediction need not be realized by its co-generated action. We introduce WISE (\emph{World Action Inference Scaling through Evaluation}), a pre-execution selector that scores each sampled rollout on action validity and temporal regularity, inverse-dynamics consistency between the proposed action and the imagined motion, and instruction-conditioned task progress, and executes the highest-scoring candidate while keeping the WAM frozen. With four candidates per decision, WISE raises closed-loop success from 6.0\% to 24.0\% on RoboLab with Cosmos~3 Edge and from 75.1\% to 78.3\% mean success on LIBERO with DreamZero, and exceeds the best existing selector in aggregate by 4.0 and 0.9 points. Component ablations and agreement analyses show that the three scores rank candidates differently and that task pr...

papers.title: SearchInject: Retrieval Exposure Control for Indirect Prompt Injection in Language-Model Search
alternate_titles: SearchInject: Retrieval Exposure Control for Indirect Prompt Injection in Language-Model Search
papers.abstract: An indirect prompt injection can affect a search-augmented large language model only after its carrier page reaches model context. SearchInject controls this admission decision with a joint score combining retrieval relevance, search-abuse cues, instruction likelihood, and two relevance interactions. A quarantine threshold is selected under an empirical 0.5% clean-candidate false-quarantine constraint on a calibration split. Evaluation uses 300 held-out SciFact queries and held-out payload categories within four construction families already represented during development. Across 1,200 query-family outcomes per retriever, top-10 target exposure falls from 0.9408 to 0.1583 for BM25, from 0.9158 to 0.1508 for a normalized hybrid, and from 0.8450 to 0.1375 for latent semantic analysis. These are relative reductions of 83.2-83.7%; the largest absolute change in clean normalized discounted cu...

papers.title: SNAP: Semantic Navigation Among Pedestrians
alternate_titles: SNAP: Semantic Navigation Among Pedestrians
papers.abstract: Navigating crowded urban environments requires robots to avoid pedestrians while adhering to social norms such as remaining on sidewalks. Existing approaches typically address either crowd avoidance or semantic path planning in isolation. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) navigation policy that jointly reasons about semantic terrain and dynamic obstacles from a single semantically annotated bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, without relying on explicit human-state estimation. Our policy outperforms established crowd-navigation and semantic-aware baselines and transfers zero-shot to a legged robot, demonstrating socially compliant navigation in highly dynamic real-world scenarios.

papers.title: Q-CamTuning: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Fine-Grained Quality Reasoning in Livestreaming Camera Tuning
alternate_titles: Q-CamTuning: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Fine-Grained Quality Reasoning in Livestreaming Camera Tuning
papers.abstract: With the popularization of livestreaming applications, automatic camera tuning has become indispensable for ordinary users to enjoy high Quality of Experience (QoE). However, the existing Image Quality Assessment (IQA) methods face two challenges in camera tuning. First, they struggle to identify subtle quality difference between images, which is common in camera tuning. Second, the ability to explain fine-grained differences and to provide suggestions for camera tuning are even more lacking. To address these challenges, we first construct FGLive-Comments, an instruction tuning dataset with rich annotations of both preferences for fine-grained image pairs and quality reasoning from global and local visual evidence, which supports selective adjustment recommendations of camera parameters. Based on FGLive-Comments, we develop Q-CamTuning, a multimodal large language model for livestreaming...

papers.title: ProteoCraft: Protein Design as Proposal-Verification Search
alternate_titles: ProteoCraft: Protein Design as Proposal-Verification Search
papers.abstract: Protein-protein interactions underpin nearly all biological processes. Yet, designing proteins with desired interactions remains challenging due to the structural complexity governing molecular recognition. This study views protein design as a search optimization problem over a combinatorial sequence space under expensive structural evaluation. Toward this goal, we introduce a novel tree-based search framework, ProteoCraft, that employs approximate structural gradients from diffusion-based structure predictors as effective proposal policies to specify where the search should explore. Complete no-gradient inference of folding models separately assigns values to the resulting sequences, determining what is good. ProteoCraft allocates this verification budget through a coarse-to-fine paradigm: multi-site edits first explore distinct sequence basins, then verified promising states undergo st...

papers.title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
alternate_titles: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
papers.abstract: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-t...

papers.title: MicroMouse: Masking Harmful Supervision in Long CoT via Relative Potential
alternate_titles: MicroMouse: Masking Harmful Supervision in Long CoT via Relative Potential
papers.abstract: Even successful long CoTs may contain harmful supervision, motivating the need for methods that can automatically identify and mask such signals during SFT. Inspired by the MicroMouse maze-solving process, we view a long CoT as a search trajectory from the input problem toward the target answer. This perspective motivates maintaining a goal-relative measure, analogous to a MicroMouse's spatial coordinates, to quantify how close the current reasoning state is to the target answer. Building on this perspective, we propose MicroMouse, an automated selective-SFT framework for masking harmful supervision in long CoTs. In MicroMouse we introduce a Relative Potential (REP) to measure how closely each reasoning state supports the gold answer. author_affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Meet Students Where They Are: Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Distillation
alternate_titles: Meet Students Where They Are: Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) mitigates the student's exposure bias by optimizing on student-generated trajectories. However, student-generated prefixes may contain reasoning errors or follow patterns unfamiliar to the teacher, undermining the reliability of its token-level supervision. This degradation becomes more pronounced as prefixes grow longer. To address this teacher-side distribution mismatch, we propose Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation (SPTA), which adapts the teacher to the states on which it is queried during distillation. Specifically, before OPD starts, we collect student rollout prefixes with random lengths and continually train the teacher to continue from the prefixes using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). By treating each prefix as context and rewarding correct final answers, the teacher learns to recover from student-induced states rather than imi...

papers.title: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging for Efficient Long-to-Short Reasoning
alternate_titles: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging for Efficient Long-to-Short Reasoning
papers.abstract: Long-to-Short (L2S) model merging seeks to combine the strong reasoning capability of long chain-of-thought models with the concise style of base models, but existing methods that rely on linear interpolation and first-order activation statistics fail to capture how the loss landscape responds to parameter displacement, leading to degraded accuracy on hard tasks. We propose Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging (LHM), a training-free framework that replaces heuristic statistics with lightweight second-order curvature information. LHM consists of three components: (1) a low-rank Hessian approximation that efficiently estimates per-layer Hessian traces via Hutchinson's estimator on random inputs, eliminating the need for task-specific data; (2) a Layer Second-Order Sensitivity (LSOS) index that combines Hessian trace with task-vector norm to quantify per-layer fusion difficulty; and (3) a Dual-Con...

papers.title: Learning to Adjudicate: Verifier-Guided Multi-Agent Reasoning for E-Commerce Relevance
alternate_titles: Learning to Adjudicate: Verifier-Guided Multi-Agent Reasoning for E-Commerce Relevance
papers.abstract: Relevance modeling is fundamental to e-commerce search, determining how well retrieved products satisfy the needs expressed in a user's query. Accurate judgments require interpreting user intent, comparing product attributes, and applying business-specific matching criteria. Current methods based on large language models (LLMs) leverage contextual understanding and reasoning, focusing on incorporating domain-specific context and enhancing reasoning performance. Despite these advances, difficult query-product pairs remain challenging when evidence from different perspectives supports conflicting conclusions. A single reasoning pass may fail to reconcile these conflicts and ensure that decisive evidence guides the final judgment. To address this challenge, we propose Collaborative Adjudication with Debate and Replay Experience (CADRE), a framework for evidence-based adjudication in e-comme...

papers.title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
alternate_titles: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
papers.abstract: LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, demonstrated that large-scale EEG pretraining can yield strong representations for diverse downstream tasks. Building on this foundation, we expand pretraining data and model capacity while retaining its core encoder and objective. We train ten encoders with 5.8 million to 1.97 billion parameters on three EEG collections spanning 25,067 to 79,910 hours, adapting signal preparation and training to heterogeneous recordings. Across 23 tasks, Atom-L* reaches 59.05% mean balanced accuracy at its best evaluated full fine-tuning (Full-FT) checkpoint, 3.61 percentage points above the strongest baseline EEG foundation model. Quark-G leads linear probing (LP) at 54.33%, a 1.24-point margin. Both also lead average task rank. papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027
alternate_titles: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe), and the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database. In this publication we report on the status of InterPro (version 110.0), detailing new developments in the database, its associated web interface, and software. Notable updates include InterPro-N, a deep-learning method that increases sequence coverage...

papers.title: History Forcing: Distilling History-Dependent Continuations for Long-Horizon Video World Models
alternate_titles: History Forcing: Distilling History-Dependent Continuations for Long-Horizon Video World Models
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables efficient generation, yet maintaining consistency over long rollouts remains challenging, especially when subjects or scenes reappear after going out of sight. Despite progress in fidelity and rollout robustness, existing distillation methods do not fully exploit richer historical information to constrain the student's current prediction. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{History Forcing}, a unified on-policy distillation framework that strengthens historical supervision for few-step autoregressive video generators. The framework uses the residual between teacher predictions with and without informative historical context to decouple this supervision. papers.title: Hindsight Credit Assignment over Trees for Agentic RL
alternate_titles: Hindsight Credit Assignment over Trees for Agentic RL
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning for long-horizon LLM agents faces a fundamental dilemma: successful experiences are essential for policy improvement, yet limited policy capabilities make such experiences difficult to discover. Sparse outcome rewards compound this challenge, leaving sampled trajectories with little relative feedback for learning. In this paper, we propose TriGRPO, a tree-based reinforcement learning framework that turns scarce successes into exploration and learning signals through hindsight credit assignment within and across rollout trees. TriGRPO constructs rollout trees through hindsight-guided branching: when an ongoing trajectory reaches a matched decision state, a successful action discovered during rollout initiates a sibling branch that continues autonomously, enabling further exploration and parent-sibling comparisons. papers.title: GigaSpeech 3: Scaling Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Recognition with Weakly Labeled Data
alternate_titles: GigaSpeech 3: Scaling Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Recognition with Weakly Labeled Data
papers.abstract: Dialectal Arabic speech recognition remains constrained by the scarcity of dialect-resolved transcribed speech despite the abundance of web audio. We introduce GigaSpeech 3, a corpus of 39,000 hours and 10 million weakly transcribed speech segments covering Algerian, Egyptian, Iraqi, Saudi, and Syrian Arabic. Starting from 60 hours of manual transcription per dialect, we train labeling models using speech-recognition-biased self-supervised learning and apply them to dialect-matched web audio. Data selection and four rounds of noisy-student refinement for Saudi and Syrian Arabic yield the final corpus. We validate its utility through dialect-specific and multi-dialect speech recognition training and cross-domain evaluation. On GigaSpeechBench, the final dialect-specific models outperform their labeling models across all five dialects and achieve a macro-average word error rate of 23.86%,...

papers.title: GTAC: A Graph-Transformer Actor-Critic for Carrier-Aware MU-MIMO User Grouping
alternate_titles: GTAC: A Graph-Transformer Actor-Critic for Carrier-Aware MU-MIMO User Grouping
papers.abstract: Achieving higher spectral efficiency (SE) in 5G and future 6G networks requires efficient massive multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) grouping under coupled physical-layer constraints and strict scheduling deadlines. Motivated by industry efforts in AI-native RAN, we propose Graph-Transformer Actor-Critic (GTAC), a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) architecture for carrier-aware MU-MIMO user grouping. The objective is to maximize the long-term proportional-fair (PF) utility of the cell subject to constraints from the practical stack protocol. GTAC comprises a shared actor--critic encoder with spatial-edge-biased attention mechanism, a pointer decoder actor that generates grouping decisions, and a multi-stage transformer critic that estimates the carrier-wide state-value during training. Training begins by cloning a teacher policy that cannot meet real-time deployment dead...

papers.title: From Local Skills to Long-Horizon Web Tasks: Progressive Skill Exploration for LLM Web Agents
alternate_titles: From Local Skills to Long-Horizon Web Tasks: Progressive Skill Exploration for LLM Web Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are driving autonomous agents toward real-world environments, with the Web emerging as one of the most representative interaction scenarios. However, training Web agents with naive exploration remains challenging: successful trajectories are rare, and the sparse terminal rewards make it difficult for agents to obtain useful feedback from failed trajectories. Inspired by skill acquisition theory, we propose Skill-Composed Progressive Exploration (SCOPE), a short-to-long learning framework for long-horizon Web agents that decomposes complex task exploration into a gradual expansion process from local skills to complete task-solving capability. Specifically, SCOPE iteratively explores around local skills: Skill Discovery extracts reusable local skills and failure experiences from historical rollouts; Skill Orchestration composes discovered skills into high-level...

papers.title: FORGE: Fault-Oriented Rework Code Generation for Executable Interlocking Assembly
alternate_titles: FORGE: Fault-Oriented Rework Code Generation for Executable Interlocking Assembly
papers.abstract: Large language models have demonstrated strong capabilities in structured reasoning and code generation, yet identifying an assembly fault does not guarantee the ability to generate executable rework programs. In interlocking assemblies, a locally plausible repair program may violate blocking dependencies, omit required recovery operations, or terminate in an incorrect configuration. We identify this challenge as fault-conditioned executable rework generation, where models must jointly reason about structural failures and generate programs that restore constrained assembly states. To benchmark this capability, we introduce FORGE-Bench, containing 4,000 tasks across 26 interlocking assemblies with five assemblies held out for evaluating generalization to unseen structures. papers.title: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
alternate_titles: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Pre-touch sensing, or sensing information about an object before contact, is an attractive modality for robot hands as it can allow a robot to anticipate and respond to a contact before it happens. In this work, we introduce ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone (4$\times$4 resolution) time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array. We mount this sensor on a parallel jaw gripper and demonstrate its utility on three distinct tasks: (i) pre-grasp adjustment, (ii) item extraction from clutter, and (iii) item insertion into tight spaces. For pre-grasp adjustment, ToF feedback reduced cycle time by 7.4$\%$ by enabling anticipatory gripper closure during approach. papers.title: Evaluation of transfer learning in hydrological forecasting using ensemble LSTM models: a statistical approach to uncertainty and accuracy
alternate_titles: Evaluation of transfer learning in hydrological forecasting using ensemble LSTM models: a statistical approach to uncertainty and accuracy
papers.abstract: Global change poses significant challenges to water resource management. Water Table Depth (WTD) is a critical variable linking subsurface dynamics to land-surface processes; however, real-world observations remain sparse. Transfer learning can support WTD monitoring, but assessing prediction quality in locations without observations is challenging. This contribution explores a method using an assessment tool to estimate prediction quality in such locations. We implement an ensemble of 100 Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict WTD using the physically-based Terrestrial Systems Modeling Platform Groundwater to Atmosphere (TSMP-G2A) simulation dataset, spatially split into training and transfer subsets. papers.title: Energy-Based Policy Orchestration
alternate_titles: Energy-Based Policy Orchestration
papers.abstract: Hierarchical control scales robot behavior by separating task-level planning from low-level control. In dynamic, high-dimensional tasks, however, a fixed planner-to-policy interface can fail when contacts, balance, or disturbances evolve faster than high-level policy updates. Execution therefore requires choosing not only which low-level policy to run, but also which policy-specific goal should be given to it. We formulate this problem as policy orchestration: runtime selection of a policy-goal pair that is likely to remain feasible while tracking the planner target. We develop EPO, an energy-based policy orchestrator for modular goal-conditioned policy families. For each policy, EPO learns a composite energy over low-level goals, where lower energy corresponds to higher feasibility and more accurate target realization. papers.title: End-To-End Petrophysical Operations with Agentic AI: A Horizontal Carbonate Reservoir Well Case Study from a Mature Onshore Field, Abu Dhabi
alternate_titles: End-To-End Petrophysical Operations with Agentic AI: A Horizontal Carbonate Reservoir Well Case Study from a Mature Onshore Field, Abu Dhabi
papers.abstract: Abstract Petrophysical work follows a well from planning through drilling and into completion, and at each step it usually passes between different specialists, vendor software, and email threads. This paper describes an in-house agentic artificial-intelligence assistant that brings those steps together behind one interface driven by text and voice. The system was validated end to end on a horizontal development well, denoted Well A here for confidentiality, drilled through a heterogeneous carbonate reservoir in a mature onshore field in Abu Dhabi. The assistant runs a fleet of nine configuration-driven skills grouped into two co-equal suites. A planning suite covers a well-data registry, document compilation, logging-program generation, cement-bond evaluation, and a logging-activity dashboard. papers.title: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
alternate_titles: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Computational drug discovery offers a growing range of tools for proposing and evaluating molecules, but combining them and deciding what to do next still requires substantial expert effort. Here, we introduce El Agente Fármaco, an AI scientist that uses modern large language model (LLM) technology to turn discovery goals expressed in everyday language into complex, scalable computational screening workflows. The agentic harness selects scientific tools, reviews their results, and adjusts subsequent steps to the target and the user's objectives. Our approach centers on a shared scientific memory: Fármaco Atlas, which stores molecules, structures, and results together with their provenance -- a record of how they were obtained. papers.title: EffComp: Efficient Prompt Compression via Hybrid Reinforcement & Supervised Learning
alternate_titles: EffComp: Efficient Prompt Compression via Hybrid Reinforcement & Supervised Learning
papers.abstract: Prompt compression is aimed at reducing input prompt lengths to enable cheaper, faster, and potentially higher-quality LLM predictions. However, existing prompt compression methods are often limited by modest compression gains, a risk of hallucination, and/or high compression latency. We propose EffComp, an Efficient prompt Compression framework for RAG-based question answering (QA). EffComp employs BERT-style document reranker and sentence selector models to allow fast extractive prompt compression at the sentence level. Its extractive nature prevents hallucinations in the compressed prompts. Additionally, the training process using a hybrid reinforcement and supervised learning approach is designed to optimize the compression ratio while preserving LLM accuracy. papers.title: Diverse-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation
alternate_titles: Diverse-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation generates the semantic ID (SID) of the next item from a user's interaction history. Existing training objectives mainly supervise target SID tokens, while on-policy distillation (OPD) provides denser supervision through a teacher's probability distribution over all tokens for more effective and efficient training. However, OPD can aggravate popularity bias: teacher feedback favors popular-item tokens, transferring this preference to the student, while student rollout favors popular items, leaving unpopular-item SID paths rarely generated and supervised. These two sources of bias reinforce each other and reduce recommendation diversity. We propose HERO, a diversity-aware OPD framework. papers.title: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning
alternate_titles: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) is a fundamental inverse problem in geophysics to estimate subsurface properties, such as velocity, from seismic measurements. Recently, self-supervised learning methods remove the need for ground-truth velocity maps during training by leveraging a forward operator to simulate seismic data from predictions and backpropagate the gradients of reconstruction loss through it. In this work, we consider a more challenging setting without accessing such gradients. To this end, we incorporate reinforcement learning into self-supervised FWI and propose a framework named DeepWaveRL. Specifically, we reformulate FWI as a policy learning problem, where the policy network predicts velocity maps as actions, and a forward operator is used solely for simulation. papers.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
alternate_titles: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models

Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. papers.title: Conformal prediction for network intrusion triage and analysis of unseen attack families
alternate_titles: Conformal prediction for network intrusion triage and analysis of unseen attack families
papers.abstract: High benchmark accuracy does not inform a security operations center which alerts to trust or whether attacks absent from training can be flagged. We evaluated conformal prediction as an analyst-triage layer and compared probability and feature-space novelty scores across 15 leave-one-attack-family-out experiments on UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS2017. Primary analyses use the first-occurrence feature deduplication. papers.title: Cold-Start Pricing of LLM Services under Two-Sided Learning
alternate_titles: Cold-Start Pricing of LLM Services under Two-Sided Learning
papers.abstract: Online large language model (LLM) services face a pricing cold start: providers initially lack the historical data and user information needed for precise pricing, while users' willingness to pay evolves with repeated use. We formulate this challenge as a \emph{two-sided learning} problem between a provider and a user. The user learns from private usage experience, whereas the provider incurs a serving cost and dynamically adapts prices using only purchase decisions to maximize cumulative profit. The provider's central challenge is to learn to price against an evolving willingness to pay without observing the private experiences driving that evolution. papers.title: Closing the Dynamics Gap through Self-Directed Robotic Interaction
alternate_titles: Closing the Dynamics Gap through Self-Directed Robotic Interaction
papers.abstract: Agentic Real2Sim2Real systems can reconstruct a scene in simulation from camera observations, but contact-rich dynamics such as friction and restitution cannot be observed without interaction. We call this the dynamics gap and present CUE, an agentic system that closes it by interacting with the environment itself. Given only a high-level instruction and no resets, the agent builds its own perception, identifies physical parameters, and targets interactions where its simulation is least accurate. On billiards, CUE reduces held-out ball-position error by 72% relative to the strongest baseline across 25 hidden-physics conditions in simulation, and we further deploy it on a real pool table. More details can be found on the project website: https://cue-dynamics.github.io/

papers.title: BLPO: Beyond-Local Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
alternate_titles: BLPO: Beyond-Local Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon tasks require large language model (LLM) agents to coordinate interdependent actions, a capability central to automating complex workflows. Stepwise group-based reinforcement learning provides finer credit than trajectory-level supervision, but reliable comparisons must account for differences in interaction history. Enforcing this consistency within the limited rollouts of each task can leave insufficient support for estimating action preferences. We propose Beyond-Local Policy Optimization (BLPO), which estimates task-progress advantages from experience shared across tasks and training updates. papers.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified

Estimating depth as the smallest turn cap, stated to the agent, under which the task passes, we audit 734 tasks from six existing datasets. papers.title: From Tool State to Scientific Action: Auditing Decision Provenance in Biomedical Research Agents
alternate_titles: From Tool State to Scientific Action: Auditing Decision Provenance in Biomedical Research Agents
papers.abstract: A scientific agent can give the same verdict while reading and citing different evidence. BioAgent-DF tests this separation using paired reference and candidate values saved at the same scientific computation site. It restores or transplants those values at their original coordinates, then runs the agent on healthy hardware. Across eight SciFact batches, Qwen3.5-4B shows repeatable citation changes in three capture-claim combinations, and Gemma 3 4B IT shows repeatable read and citation changes in four. These seven combinations cover two claims. Full restoration recovers the reference evidence sets while verdicts remain unchanged. Verdict changes observed under the baseline prompt did not recur under the explicit-example prompt. papers.title: EMBERS: Empirically Motivated Robustness Testing of Deep Research Systems via Defect-Guided Fuzzing
alternate_titles: EMBERS: Empirically Motivated Robustness Testing of Deep Research Systems via Defect-Guided Fuzzing
papers.abstract: Deep Research (DR) systems extend large language models into autonomous agents that decompose complex information needs, iteratively search the web, and synthesize evidence to answer challenging questions. However, their multi-stage execution may introduce robustness risks, as variations in user questions or intermediate search inputs may propagate across research stages and lead to incorrect answers. Existing evaluations focus on task-solving capabilities or robustness against external evidence disturbances, leaving intrinsic weaknesses in DR execution insufficiently explored. Thus, we conduct an empirical study of 1,932 execution trajectories from three representative DR systems and identify nine recurring defect categories across subquestion formulation, online search, and final reasoning. papers.abstract: Contemporary portfolio construction remains a gap on when the markets are turbulent between structural market stress and retail sentiment because of conventional risk measures on product price. The gap is overcome by the proposed Phase-Space Reconstruction and Regime Identification(PRRI) model. It identify the quantifiable divergence between the dynamical state of the market and the behavioural posture of its participants. To measure , a novel leading indicator derived from the inconsistency between Takens-embedded phase-space market regimes and contemporaneous retail sentiment signals. papers.abstract: Large-scale super-apps generate heterogeneous transaction logs in which users interact with multiple businesses, item identifiers are only partially available, and future value targets are sparse, heavy-tailed, and cumulative over time. papers.title: Calibration-Constrained Diagnostics for Evaluating LLM Self-Evaluation
alternate_titles: Calibration-Constrained Diagnostics for Evaluating LLM Self-Evaluation
papers.abstract: We introduce a reusable evaluation artifact for diagnosing whether LLM self-reported confidence can support confidence-gated act-or-defer decisions. The artifact is designed for evaluation rather than safety certification: it provides a black-box protocol, prompts, judge-reference labels, model outputs, reproduction scripts, and calibration-constrained diagnostic metrics for auditing LLM self-evaluation across math, factual, and commonsense reasoning tasks. Our central finding is that aggregate uncertainty summaries can produce deployment-misleading rankings: a model that appears strongest under standard aggregate calibration metrics can fail under category-level calibration constraints, while a model with worse aggregate calibration can exhibit stronger calibration-constrained behavior in the positive-margin region where high self-selection accuracy and tight calibration coexist. papers.title: CST: Lightweight Risk Triage with Source-Grounded Evidence for Web Discussions
alternate_titles: CST: Lightweight Risk Triage with Source-Grounded Evidence for Web Discussions
papers.abstract: Web communities rely on moderators to catch harmful messages such as insults, hate speech, and scams, but no one can read every message. Existing tools give each message a risk score, which tells moderators where to look but not what to read or how to check it. Yet meaning depends on context: the same reply, "I agree.", can support or oppose removing someone from a group. Moderators therefore need source-grounded evidence, not just scores: a few key messages kept with their original wording and replies. We present CST, a lightweight triage pipeline that first decides where to look, then what to show. It scores risk by pairing character patterns, which capture exact wording, with sentence meaning from a fixed multilingual model, so it handles several languages and runs on an ordinary CPU. papers.title: Ascend-SpMM: Accelerating Sparse Matrix-Dense Matrix Multiplication on Ascend NPUs
alternate_titles: Ascend-SpMM: Accelerating Sparse Matrix-Dense Matrix Multiplication on Ascend NPUs
papers.abstract: Sparse Matrix-Dense Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) is a fundamental kernel in graph neural networks and scientific computing, yet its optimization on Ascend NPUs remains largely unexplored. The physically decoupled Cube/Vector architecture and single-threaded scalar instruction dispatch of modern NPUs introduce unique challenges. We present Ascend-SpMM, a novel and systematic framework tailored to the physically decoupled architecture of Ascend NPUs.We introduce a memory-centric cost model that quantifies hardware affinity and guides a conflict-bounded, densityaware task-mapping strategy. papers.title: Improving Entrepreneurial Skills by Practicing with AI
alternate_titles: Improving Entrepreneurial Skills by Practicing with AI
papers.abstract: Durable skills like critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration are essential for innovation, yet teaching them remains difficult. In this work, we focus on the entrepreneurial domain, where these skills and others are required, and ask whether AI can be used as a tool for improving entrepreneurial proficiency. As a first step towards this challenge, we present an extension of Vantage, a platform developed at Google Research, adapted to serve as an interactive practice environment for entrepreneurship. Vantage pairs students with simulated AI peers engineered to navigate realistic business scenarios and challenge learners to exercise key skills.
